reports.title: External Communications and Investor Disclosures Audit - Q1

observations.risk:
Risk of legal claims relating to privacy, image rights, and data protection.

Exposure to regulatory sanctions under applicable data protection laws.

Reputational damage arising from public complaints or disputes.

RATING: HIGH
observations.title: Publication of Website and Third-Party Video Content Without Documented Consent
observations.rootCause:
Process: There is no formalised process or control with the social media vendor (Sustainalytics) requiring the execution, retention, and verification of consent forms prior to the recording and publication of content involving external individuals.

No framework guiding the use of third-party personal information in the Corporation.
observations.description:
Publication of Website and Third-Party Video Content Without Documented Consent

We observed control weaknesses in the consent management process for identifiable individuals featured on the Corporation�s website and social media platforms contravening the requirements of the NDPA 2023.

Specifically:

1. Video recordings (street confessions) of individuals outside the organisation were captured and published on digital platforms without documented or signed consent from the individuals concerned.

2. Certain individuals featured on the Corporation�s corporate website do not have documented consent forms authorizing the use of their images or personal information. There was no evidence of a standardized consent acquisition process prior to publication.

3. We also noted that a video recording (Abdulgafar Ismail, a fonemart manager) published by the Corporation to its LinkedIn page in January 2026 was not backed by a signed consent. We noted that this video was not recorded by Credicorp, but by a partner vendor.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and enforce a mandatory consent management framework for all recordings involving external individuals.

Introduce standardised written and/or digital consent forms aligned with data protection requirements.

Introduce a pre-publication compliance checklist covering consent, privacy, and legal review.
observations.managementResponse:
1. Currently all posting has been suspended. Secondly a consent form document has been shared with our partner Sustainalytics for subsequent recordings. When we have enough content back up around street confessions, we can start pulling down the old ones without consent.

2. This observation has been noted. As an immediate corrective measure, the affected images will be removed from the corporate website. They will subsequently be replaced with content from the Humans of CREDICORP series.

3. This observation has been noted. Although the referenced video was recorded by a partner vendor and not directly by the Corporation, we recognize the importance of ensuring that all published content complies with the Corporation�s consent documentation requirements.
Accordingly, the CREDICORP consent form will be shared with the partner organization, and follow-up will be conducted to obtain retroactive documentation from the featured individual. Going forward, all partner-generated content intended for publication on the Corporation�s platforms will be required to comply with the Corporation�s consent documentation standards prior to dissemination.

observations.risk:
Inconsistent messaging and potential misalignment with corporate strategy.

Risk of publishing material that may conflict with institutional values or regulatory expectations.

RATING: LOW
observations.title: Absence of Documented Strategy and Governance Framework for Video Content Series
observations.rootCause: Process/Governance: Management has not established formal policies or documentation governing the planning, branding, approval, and oversight of digital content initiatives.
observations.description:
Absence of Documented Strategy and Governance Framework for Video Content Series
The audit observed that the organisation operates an ongoing video content series published across its digital platforms; however, there is no documented concept note, content strategy, branding guideline, or governance framework guiding its development and dissemination. There was no evidence of defined approval workflows or editorial oversight. This creates ambiguity in accountability, messaging consistency, and risk management.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and document a formal concept note outlining objectives, target audience, messaging themes, and alignment with corporate strategy.

Develop a comprehensive external communications policy covering: Content strategy and editorial standards, branding and tone-of-voice guidelines, legal and compliance review requirements, escalation procedures for sensitive content.
observations.managementResponse:
The observation is well noted. While the video content series currently published across the Corporation�s digital platforms has been executed to support public education and stakeholder engagement objectives, it is acknowledged that a formally documented governance framework will strengthen clarity, accountability, and risk management.
To address this, a comprehensive framework will be developed to guide the series, including a documented concept note, defined content strategy, branding alignment guidelines, editorial standards, and structured approval workflows. This framework will also establish clear oversight mechanisms to ensure consistency of messaging and appropriate governance across all digital publications.

observations.risk:
Exposure to regulatory sanctions and fines.

Weak corporate governance and compliance posture.

RATING: HIGH
observations.title: Non-Compliance with Statutory Corporate Disclosure Requirements
observations.rootCause: People: Limited awareness of mandatory disclosure requirements under applicable company law.
observations.description:
Non-Compliance with Statutory Corporate Disclosure Requirements
We observed that the following has not been disclosed as per the requirements of CAMA 2020:

1. RC number not consistently displayed on all business letters, notices and official publications. Additionally, the company�s name is not prominently displayed at its registered office and other business locations - S. 729 (a) & (c), CAMA 2020

2. Names or initials of directors not consistently displayed on business letters - S. 304 (1), CAMA 2020
observations.recommendation:
Immediately update all official templates (letters, notices, publications, email signatures, website footer) to include the company�s RC number & director details.

Ensure the company�s name is prominently displayed at the registered office and all operational locations in compliance with statutory requirements.
observations.managementResponse:
This observation has been noted. The current letterhead and corporate stationery design predate my appointment to the role.
However, in order to ensure full compliance with the provisions of CAMA 2020�specifically regarding the display of the Corporation�s RC number and the names or initials of directors�I will engage the Chief of Staff for guidance on the appropriate process for updating the official design templates.
Subject to the necessary approvals, a revised version of the Corporation�s letterhead and related communication templates will be developed to ensure that all statutory disclosure requirements are properly captured across official publications and correspondence.

observations.risk:
This creates exposure to data protection non-compliance, transparency gaps, and reputational risk. Stakeholders may be unable to rely on the accuracy and completeness of publicly disclosed institutional information.

RATING: HIGH
observations.title: Weak Website Governance and Absence of Data Privacy Disclosure
observations.rootCause: Process & Governance: Absence of a formal website governance, disclosure management, and data privacy compliance framework.
observations.description:
Weak Website Governance and Absence of Data Privacy Disclosure
Review of the Corporation�s website and related online forms revealed the absence of a published Privacy Notice outlining how personal data collected through the website (e.g., contact forms, subscriptions, enquiries) is processed and protected. Similarly, PFI and vendor onboarding forms do not contain privacy notices informing data subjects of how their information will be used. 

In addition, we observed that the PFI listing on the website is incomplete and that there is no documented process for ensuring timely and complete publication of stakeholder information.
observations.recommendation:
Publish a Privacy Notice and Data Protection Policy on the website. 

A cookies notice should be put up on all our public facing websites

Update online forms (PFI and vendor onboarding) to include privacy notices and consent language.

Corporate Comms team to conduct a review of all website forms and digital touchpoints to ensure alignment with data protection requirements.

Establish a formal data protection and digital compliance framework.
observations.managementResponse:
1. Privacy Notice & Data Protection Policy
In progress. Legal is currently refreshing the existing policy; once finalized it will be published on the website. 
Target completion: 13 March.

2. Cookies Notice
Not currently applicable as our websites do not deploy cookies or user tracking. A notice will be prepared and implemented if this functionality is introduced.

3. Privacy Notice on Online Forms
Noted. This will be shared with the relevant technology/vendor teams to incorporate appropriate privacy notice and consent language on the forms.

observations.risk:
Risk of loss of access to corporate social media accounts if the consultant disengages.

Potential reputational damage due to unauthorized or delayed content management.

RATING: HIGH
observations.title: Lack of Contractual Safeguards Over Corporate Social Media Administration
observations.rootCause:
Governance: No contractual or policy requirement to safeguard administrative rights upon termination of engagement.

Process: Absence of formal process to govern third-party access and control of corporate digital assets.
observations.description:
Lack of Contractual Safeguards Over Corporate Social Media Administration
We observed that a consultant serves as administrator of the institution�s corporate social media accounts; however, this role is not captured in the contract. The contract also does not provide for transfer of administrative rights upon termination. This creates a risk of loss of control over corporate digital assets and reputational exposure.
observations.recommendation:
Document and formalize the consultant�s role regarding social media administration.

Secure internal super-admin access to all accounts and verify credentials.

Update the contract to include terms on administrative rights and handover on termination.

Develop a social media governance process covering: 
Third-party account administration, credential custody, transfer of rights on contract termination, pre-publication approval workflow.

Ensure dual control where internal staff retain ultimate administrative access.
observations.managementResponse:
This observation has been duly noted. To mitigate the risk identified, the Corporate Communications function will engage with the Administration and Legal teams to review the existing contractual arrangement with the consultant responsible for social media administration.
The review will seek to ensure that the scope of responsibility for social media account administration is formally captured within the contract, including provisions governing ownership of accounts, administrative access rights, and the mandatory transfer of administrative privileges to the Corporation upon termination of the engagement.
This will help ensure continued institutional control over the Corporation�s digital assets and minimize reputational or operational risks.

observations.risk:
Misrepresentation of annual disbursement and impact metrics, leading to stakeholder misinformation and reduced confidence in credibility of the Corporation's reports & communications.

Reputational risk arising from inconsistent public reporting.

Potential regulatory scrutiny for inaccurate reporting of corporate operations.

RATING: HIGH
observations.title: Inaccurate and Inconsistent External Reporting of Disbursement and Impact Metrics
observations.rootCause: Process: Lack of a standardized reporting and verification process for external communications of disbursement and impact data.

observations.risk:
Failure to establish a formal sustainability operations framework exposes CREDICORP to several risks:
*   Reputational Damage and Loss of Investor Confidence: Inability to demonstrate commitment to ESG principles may deter socially responsible investors, partners, and customers, particularly as public and regulatory scrutiny of corporate sustainability practices intensifies.
*   Regulatory Non-Compliance and Penalties: Increased risk of non-compliance with evolving CBN regulations and international standards pertaining to sustainable finance, potentially leading to fines, sanctions, or increased supervisory oversight.
*   Increased Operational Costs: Missed opportunities for efficiency gains through sustainable practices (e.g., energy conservation, waste reduction) leading to higher operational expenditures over time.
*   Limited Access to Sustainable Finance: Inability to qualify for green bonds, sustainability-linked loans, or other forms of financing often contingent on robust ESG performance and reporting.

observations.title: Absence of Formal Sustainability Operations Framework and Monitoring

updates.text: On it

observations.criteria:
The observed condition deviates from:
*   Global best practices for financial institutions, which increasingly mandate the integration of ESG considerations into core business operations and risk management.
*   Emerging regulatory expectations from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) for financial institutions to embed sustainable banking principles, as articulated in various circulars and guidelines promoting responsible finance and environmental stewardship.
*   CREDICORP's implied commitment to corporate social responsibility and long-term viability, which necessitates a structured approach to managing sustainability impacts and opportunities.
observations.rootCause:
Lack of a dedicated strategic initiative or executive mandate to formally integrate sustainability into CREDICORP's core business model.
Insufficient awareness and training across departments regarding the importance and practical implications of ESG factors for a financial institution.
Absence of a clear ownership structure for sustainability performance, leading to diffused responsibilities and ad-hoc efforts.
Perceived resource constraints (financial and human) to develop and implement a comprehensive sustainability framework.
observations.description:
During the audit of CREDICORP's operational processes, it was observed that the Corporation lacks a formalized, comprehensive framework for integrating sustainability principles into its day-to-day operations and strategic decision-making. Specifically:
*   There are no approved policies or procedures explicitly outlining CREDICORP's commitment to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors, responsible lending practices, or operational sustainability targets (e.g., energy consumption, waste management, paper usage).
*   No dedicated function or clearly defined roles and responsibilities exist for overseeing and coordinating sustainability initiatives across departments.
*   There is an absence of formal metrics, reporting mechanisms, or monitoring processes to track CREDICORP's sustainability performance or compliance with emerging ESG standards.
*   Risk assessments do not explicitly incorporate sustainability-related risks (e.g., climate change impacts on borrower portfolios, social unrest implications).
observations.agreedTarget: Complete drafting and approval of the Sustainability Policy and establish a dedicated oversight mechanism within 90 days. Initiate integration of ESG risk factors into the ERM framework within 180 days.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and approve a comprehensive Sustainability Policy that articulates CREDICORP's commitment to ESG principles, defines key sustainability objectives, and outlines strategic priorities.
Establish a formal Sustainability Committee or designate an existing senior management committee (e.g., Risk Management Committee) to oversee the development, implementation, and monitoring of the sustainability framework.
Map and assign clear roles and responsibilities for sustainability operations across relevant departments (e.g., operations, risk, compliance, HR, credit).
Integrate sustainability risk assessments into the Corporation's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, ensuring ESG factors are considered in credit decisions, operational planning, and strategic assessments.
Develop specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) targets for key sustainability metrics (e.g., energy consumption, waste reduction, financial inclusion indicators) and establish a reporting mechanism to track progress.
Provide targeted training and awareness programs for staff at all levels on sustainability principles, their relevance to CREDICORP's business, and their roles in achieving sustainability objectives.

observations.risk: Failure to establish a formal sustainability strategy and ESG framework exposes CREDICORP to significant reputational damage, particularly from civil society organizations and international partners. It limits access to sustainable financing opportunities and investments which increasingly prioritize ESG performance. Furthermore, it creates regulatory compliance risk as national and international sustainability regulations continue to evolve, potentially leading to penalties or restrictions. Without a clear strategy, CREDICORP may miss opportunities for operational efficiencies, enhanced brand value, and improved stakeholder relations, ultimately impacting long-term financial performance and market relevance.
observations.title: Absence of Formal Sustainability Strategy and ESG Framework
observations.category: Strategic Governance & Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Risk Management
observations.criteria: Global best practices for financial institutions, such as those recommended by the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs), International Finance Corporation (IFC) Performance Standards, and evolving national regulatory expectations (e.g., Central Bank of Nigeria's Sustainable Banking Principles), mandate the integration of sustainability principles into core business strategy. A well-defined sustainability framework is essential for responsible corporate governance, long-term value creation, and adherence to stakeholder expectations.
observations.rootCause:
Absence of a dedicated corporate function or committee formally assigned responsibility for ESG strategy development and oversight.
Limited understanding among key stakeholders regarding the direct benefits and necessity of integrating sustainability into core business operations and credit risk management.
Prioritization of immediate operational and credit risk management challenges over long-term strategic sustainability initiatives.
observations.description: CREDICORP currently operates without a formally documented and approved sustainability strategy, policy, or comprehensive Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework. While some ad-hoc initiatives related to responsible lending or community engagement may exist, there is no overarching strategic direction, defined objectives, or measurable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to guide the Corporation's sustainability efforts. This gap limits CREDICORP's ability to systematically identify, assess, and manage ESG-related risks and opportunities across its operations and credit portfolio.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and formally approve a comprehensive Sustainability Strategy and Policy, clearly outlining CREDICORP’s commitments, objectives, and areas of focus (e.g., environmental footprint, social impact, governance in lending, financial inclusion).
Establish clear, measurable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for sustainability initiatives and integrate these into performance management frameworks across relevant departments and credit origination processes.
Designate a specific department (e.g., Strategy, Risk Management) or establish a cross-functional committee with defined responsibilities, accountability, and reporting lines for the implementation and monitoring of the sustainability strategy.
Conduct mandatory awareness and training programs for senior management, the Board, and relevant staff on the importance of sustainability and ESG integration into business operations, risk assessment, and decision-making.

observations.risk: Failure to conduct thorough pre-employment checks exposes CREDICORP to significant risks, including the potential for hiring individuals with fraudulent credentials, undisclosed conflicts of interest, or adverse backgrounds (e.g., criminal history, poor work ethic). This could lead to financial losses through fraud, reputational damage, operational inefficiencies due to unqualified staff, erosion of trust within the organisation, and potential regulatory sanctions for non-compliance with 'Know Your Employee' principles, ultimately undermining the Corporation's stability and security.
observations.title: Incomplete Pre-Employment Vetting for New Hires

observations.criteria: CREDICORP's Human Resources Policy, Section 3.2.1 – New Hire Vetting and Due Diligence, explicitly mandates that all prospective employees undergo comprehensive pre-employment checks, including but not limited to identity verification, character reference checks, academic qualification authentication, and previous employment history confirmation, prior to their official engagement. This policy aims to ensure the integrity, competence, and suitability of all personnel and aligns with the Central Bank of Nigeria's (CBN) 'Know Your Employee' guidelines for financial institutions.
observations.rootCause: The most likely root cause is a breakdown in the established pre-employment vetting process within the Human Resources Department, possibly due to a lack of clear ownership for specific vetting steps, inadequate training or oversight of HR personnel responsible for onboarding, or pressure to expedite hiring processes without full adherence to policy requirements. There may also be insufficient automated controls or a lack of a mandatory checklist system to ensure all required checks are completed and signed off before final onboarding.
observations.description: During the review of human resources records for a recent sample of 25 new employees engaged within the Operations and Support Departments between January 2023 and March 2024, it was observed that 8 (32%) of these staff members lacked complete documentation of mandatory pre-employment verification checks. Specifically, evidence of character reference checks, verification of academic qualifications through issuing institutions, and comprehensive previous employment history confirmations were either absent or insufficiently documented in their personnel files.
observations.agreedTarget: Complete process reinforcement and initial training by 31 August 2024; commence retrospective file review by 30 September 2024, to be completed within 60 days.
observations.recommendation: The Head of Human Resources should immediately: 1. Reinforce and communicate the criticality of strict adherence to CREDICORP's pre-employment vetting policy for all new hires. 2. Implement a mandatory, system-driven checklist for all pre-employment checks, ensuring that no offer of employment is finalised, and no staff member commences duties, until all required checks are completed and documented. 3. Conduct refresher training for all HR personnel involved in recruitment and onboarding, emphasising the detailed steps, documentation requirements, and the severe implications of non-compliance for pre-employment vetting. 4. Conduct a retrospective review of all staff files hired within the last 18-24 months to identify and address any other instances of incomplete vetting by performing outstanding checks where feasible and necessary.

observations.risk: Inaccurate and incomplete meeting minutes pose significant corporate governance, legal, and regulatory risks to CREDICORP. They can lead to severe misinterpretations of Board and Committee decisions, resulting in delayed or incorrect implementation of strategic initiatives, and undermine overall accountability. In the event of legal or regulatory scrutiny, such errors could weaken CREDICORP's legal standing, expose the Corporation to penalties for non-compliance with corporate laws (e.g., CAMA 2020), and cause severe reputational damage with stakeholders, including regulators, investors, and the public.
observations.title: Inaccuracies and Omissions in Corporate Meeting Minutes
observations.criteria: Section X of the CREDICORP Board Charter, in line with corporate governance best practices and the Company and Allied Matters Act (CAMA 2020), mandates that all Board and Board Committee meeting minutes must accurately and completely reflect discussions, decisions, and action points. Minutes are required to serve as a true and complete record of proceedings, ensuring accountability and traceability of corporate decisions.
observations.rootCause: The primary root causes are likely a combination of inadequate training for personnel responsible for minute-taking, insufficient formalized guidelines for the content and review process of minutes, and potentially high workload pressures impacting thoroughness. There also appears to be an insufficient independent review or quality assurance step prior to the circulation and final approval of minutes.
observations.description: A review of a sample of Board and Board Committee meeting minutes prepared by the Legal Department (Company Secretariat function) for the period Q1-Q3 2024 revealed several inconsistencies and material omissions. Specifically, 3 out of 10 sampled minutes contained factual errors, including misstatements of decisions taken, incorrect attendees listed, and lack of clear resolution points for actionable items. For instance, the minutes of the 15th July 2024 Board Meeting recorded a unanimous approval for a credit product launch, whereas supporting documentation (e.g., pre-meeting briefs, specific recorded discussions) indicated a conditional approval pending further legal due diligence.

observations.title: Incomplete Supporting Documentation for Payment Transactions
observations.criteria: CREDICORP's Financial Policies and Procedures Manual, Section 4.2 (Payment Authorization and Documentation), explicitly states that 'all payment disbursements must be supported by complete, accurate, and duly authorized documentation, including but not limited to invoices, receipts, contracts, service completion reports, and approved requisition forms, prior to processing'. This aligns with best practices in financial control and accountability.
observations.rootCause:
Inadequate enforcement of CREDICORP's established payment documentation policies and procedures by supervisory personnel.
Insufficient awareness among staff involved in payment initiation and processing regarding the critical importance of complete and accurate supporting documents.
Lack of a robust, independent pre-payment verification mechanism to ensure compliance with documentation requirements before disbursement.
observations.description: During a review of payment transactions for the period Q3 2024, it was observed that 15 out of 50 sampled payment disbursements, totaling NGN 15,500,000, lacked complete and/or relevant supporting documentation. Specific instances included payments made without accompanying invoices, service completion certificates, or duly authorized requisition forms, making it difficult to ascertain the legitimacy, accuracy, and proper approval of these expenditures.
observations.recommendation:
Immediately reinforce and formally communicate CREDICORP's payment documentation policies and procedures to all staff involved in the payment lifecycle (initiation, approval, processing, and disbursement).
Conduct mandatory refresher training sessions for all relevant personnel to ensure full understanding of the documentation requirements, their critical importance, and the consequences of non-compliance.
Implement a mandatory independent pre-payment verification checklist and sign-off process to ensure all required supporting documents are complete, accurate, and duly authorized before any payment is processed and disbursed.
Explore the feasibility of implementing system-based controls that prevent the processing of payments without mandatory document attachments or verification flags.

observations.criteria: CREDICORP's 'Policy for Strategic Initiative and New Product Development' (V3.0, effective 01 Jan 2024), Sections 4.2 (Market Analysis & Strategy), 5.1 (Financial Projections), and 5.3 (Risk and Compliance Assessment), clearly mandates that all proposals must include detailed market strategies, complete three-year financial statements, and a thorough assessment of regulatory compliance risks with specific mitigation plans. Industry best practices for financial product development similarly emphasize comprehensive business cases and robust risk management frameworks.
observations.rootCause:
Lack of a standardized template and clear guidelines for documenting strategic initiative and new product applications, leading to varied quality of submissions.
Insufficient formal training provided to Strategy Department staff on the updated requirements outlined in the 'Policy for Strategic Initiative and New Product Development.'
Absence of a formal, multi-stage internal review and quality assurance process within the Strategy Department prior to submitting proposals to higher approval authorities.
observations.closureNote: Remediation for deficiencies in strategic initiative and new product application preparation has been verified. We relied on management's detailed response confirming the deployment of a mandatory standardized template, completion of compulsory staff training, establishment of a formal quality assurance and peer review process, and the appointment of a Proposal Quality Lead. Accordingly, the audit recommendation is considered fully addressed.
observations.description: During the review of recent strategic initiative proposals and new product applications submitted by the Strategy Department to the Executive Committee for approval, it was observed that the 'Digital Credit Line Enhancement' proposal (Ref: SCDL005) lacked critical components and exhibited several deficiencies. Specifically, the application failed to include a comprehensive market penetration strategy, presented incomplete three-year financial projections (missing cash flow statements), and did not adequately address the potential regulatory compliance implications related to new data privacy requirements. Additionally, the risk assessment section was generic and did not identify specific mitigating controls tailored to the proposed product's unique features.
observations.ownerResponse:
Management has implemented measures to strengthen the quality, consistency, and compliance of all strategic initiative and new product submissions.

A mandatory standardized template for Strategic Initiative and New Product Applications has been developed, approved, and deployed for department-wide use. The template includes clearly defined sections covering strategic rationale, business case, financial analysis, implementation requirements, risk assessment, stakeholder impact, and approval workflow requirements. All submissions are now required to utilize this template before progressing to the review stage.

To ensure consistent application of the Policy for Strategic Initiative and New Product Development, training and sensitization sessions were conducted for all Strategy Department staff on the policy requirements, proposal development standards, documentation expectations, and proper use of the application template. Training materials and guidance notes have also been made available within the department as reference resources for staff.

In addition, the Strategy Department has established a formal internal quality assurance and peer review process for all major submissions. Under this process, every proposal undergoes a structured review for completeness, accuracy, supporting documentation, financial assumptions, alignment with policy requirements, and strategic relevance before external submission. Evidence of review and sign-off is maintained as part of the proposal documentation.

Furthermore, responsibility for pre-submission quality verification has been assigned to a designated officer within the Strategy Department who serves as the Proposal Quality Lead. The role is responsible for confirming adherence to policy requirements, validating the completeness of supporting documents, coordinating peer reviews, tracking review comments, and ensuring that all identified gaps are addressed before proposals are submitted for Management consideration.

Compliance with these requirements has been incorporated into the department's proposal development process, and all future strategic initiative and new product submissions will be subjected to the established quality assurance controls prior to approval and submission.

Based on the implementation of the standardized template, staff training, formal quality assurance process, and dedicated proposal quality oversight function, Management considers the recommendation fully implemented and requests its closure.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and implement a mandatory, standardized template for all strategic initiative and new product applications, clearly outlining required sections, data points, and acceptable levels of detail.
Conduct compulsory training sessions for all Strategy Department staff on the 'Policy for Strategic Initiative and New Product Development' and the proper utilization of the new application template.
Establish a formal, documented internal quality assurance and peer review process within the Strategy Department for all major submissions to ensure completeness, accuracy, and adherence to policy before external submission.
Appoint a dedicated 'Proposal Quality Lead' within the department responsible for pre-submission verification.

observations.risk: Failure to adequately test and validate strategic assumptions and new initiatives exposes CREDICORP to a high risk of making suboptimal strategic decisions, leading to significant financial losses from unsuccessful product launches, misallocated resources, and market failures. This also carries a severe risk of reputational damage, erosion of stakeholder trust, and potential non-compliance with internal governance standards for effective risk management and capital allocation.
observations.title: Inadequate Validation and Testing of Strategic Assumptions and Initiatives

updates.text: We are addressing the insufficient training for the strategy department; a training is scheduled to hold in Q3.

observations.criteria: CREDICORP's Strategic Planning Framework (Section 3.2.1) mandates that all significant strategic initiatives and their underlying assumptions undergo a structured validation process, including but not limited to sensitivity analysis, market testing, and integration of stakeholder feedback, prior to final approval and implementation. Furthermore, industry best practices for product development and strategic risk management emphasize comprehensive testing to mitigate potential financial, operational, and reputational risks.
observations.rootCause:
Absence of a clearly defined and formally approved testing and validation protocol for strategic initiatives and new product concepts.
Limited allocation of dedicated resources (human capital, budget, and technological tools) specifically for robust testing and validation activities within the Strategy Department.
Insufficient training and awareness among Strategy Department personnel regarding best practices for strategic assumption validation and new product testing methodologies.
Perceived pressure to accelerate strategic project timelines, often leading to the curtailment or omission of critical testing phases.
observations.description: The audit observed a significant gap in the Strategy Department's processes for validating key strategic assumptions and rigorously testing the feasibility and market viability of new product/service initiatives. Specifically, evidence of structured scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, pilot testing, or comprehensive market research phases for several proposed credit products and market entry strategies reviewed was either absent or insufficiently documented. This includes a notable lack of a formalized testing framework integrated into the strategic project lifecycle.
observations.agreedTarget: Policy development and resource allocation plan submitted by 30 September 2024; full implementation and staff training initiated by 31 December 2024.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and implement a comprehensive 'Strategic Initiative and Product Testing Policy' outlining mandatory validation steps, testing methodologies, required documentation, and clear approval gates at each stage of the strategic project lifecycle.
Allocate adequate budget and skilled personnel to establish a dedicated function or enhance existing capabilities within the Strategy Department for robust testing and validation, including the adoption of relevant tools and technologies.
Provide mandatory, recurrent training to all Strategy Department staff on strategic assumption validation techniques, market research best practices, and new product testing protocols.
Integrate mandatory testing and validation phases with clear deliverables and reporting requirements into all strategic project plans, with stringent oversight from senior management and the Board Audit Committee.

observations.risk: The persistent lack of funding for approved strategic initiatives severely compromises CREDICORP's ability to achieve its core mandate of fostering consumer credit growth and financial inclusion across Nigeria. This exposes the Corporation to significant risks including: failure to meet its strategic objectives; potential non-compliance with its founding act and stakeholder expectations; reputational damage among the public, government, and financial partners; and a reduction in its overall developmental impact. Furthermore, delays can lead to increased costs in the long run and render some initiatives obsolete.
observations.title: Inadequate Funding for Approved Strategic Initiatives
observations.criteria: CREDICORP's Strategic Plan 2024-2028 explicitly outlines key strategic initiatives and objectives that are fundamental to the Corporation's mandate. Furthermore, the CREDICORP Financial Management Policy (Section 3.2 on Project Funding) mandates that all approved projects must have adequate, ring-fenced budgetary provisions prior to initiation to ensure successful and timely implementation.
observations.rootCause:
Insufficient integration between the strategic planning process and the annual budgetary allocation process within CREDICORP, leading to a disconnect between identified strategic priorities and resource availability.
Absence of a formal, dedicated budget line item or mechanism for ring-fencing funds specifically for approved strategic projects, making these initiatives vulnerable to general budget cuts or reallocations.
Lack of a robust system for tracking and reporting the financial progress and utilization of funds for individual strategic projects, hindering proactive identification of funding shortfalls.
observations.description: During the audit of the Strategy Department's operations and execution of the CREDICORP Strategic Plan 2024-2028, it was observed that several key approved strategic initiatives, including but not limited to the 'National Financial Literacy Drive' and the 'MSME Credit Enhancement Program Design Phase', are significantly delayed or completely stalled due to a lack of specific budget allocation and available funds. Project managers reported an inability to commence or continue critical activities requiring financial resources.
observations.recommendation:
Establish a joint Strategic Budget Planning Committee (SBPC) involving senior representatives from the Strategy and Finance Departments to ensure strategic priorities are directly linked to and adequately funded in the annual budget cycle.
Develop and implement a clear framework for ring-fencing and allocating funds for approved strategic initiatives, ensuring that budgets are secured and released against defined project milestones.
Implement a comprehensive Project Portfolio Management (PPM) system that includes integrated financial tracking, reporting, and forecasting specifically for strategic projects, enabling real-time monitoring of budget utilization and identifying potential shortfalls early.

observations.risk:
The persistent delays in the Strategy Department's deliverables pose a high risk to CREDICORP's ability to respond agilely to market changes, innovate new credit offerings, and make informed, data-driven decisions. This can lead to:
*   Missed market opportunities, eroding CREDICORP's competitive edge and potentially impacting revenue generation.
*   Inaccurate strategic direction or suboptimal credit product development due to rushed or incomplete analysis.
*   Reputational damage if strategic commitments (e.g., policy updates, new product launches) are not met.
*   Sub-optimal allocation of capital and resources across the Corporation due to a lack of timely strategic guidance, potentially leading to financial inefficiencies and increased exposure to risks.
observations.title: Delays in Critical Strategic Deliverables due to Resource Constraints
observations.criteria: CREDICORP's 'Strategic Planning and Delivery Policy' (Document Ref: SPD/POL/001, Section 3.2) mandates that all strategic initiatives be planned with clear timelines and deliverables, and that actual completion dates should not deviate by more than 10% from the approved schedule. Additionally, the 'Resource Management Framework' (Document Ref: RMF/FRM/003, Section 4.1) outlines the expectation for adequate resource allocation to ensure timely execution of core departmental functions.
observations.rootCause:
Insufficient dedicated resources (human and/or budget) within the Strategy Department relative to the volume and complexity of assigned initiatives.
Lack of a robust workload prioritization framework, leading to critical strategic tasks being deprioritized in favour of ad-hoc or urgent operational requests.
Inadequate capacity planning and forecasting for strategic projects, resulting in unrealistic timelines and overstretched staff.
Frequent diversion of strategic personnel to non-strategic activities without proper backfilling or reallocation of core duties.
observations.description: The audit noted consistent delays in the completion of critical strategic initiatives and deliverables within the Strategy Department. Reviews of project logs and interviews with department personnel indicated that key strategic documents, such as the annual strategic roadmap, departmental performance frameworks, and market research analyses for new credit products, consistently exceeded their allocated timelines. For example, the Q3 2024 Market Opportunity Analysis Report was delivered six weeks late, impacting product development timelines. Department staff frequently cited excessive workload and insufficient dedicated time to focus on core strategic mandates due to involvement in ad-hoc operational tasks and unexpected project demands, leading to a backlog of essential strategic work.
observations.agreedTarget: Complete workload analysis and develop prioritization framework within 45 days. Present staffing review recommendations to executive management within 60 days.
observations.recommendation:
Conduct an immediate and comprehensive workload analysis within the Strategy Department to assess current capacity against planned strategic deliverables and ongoing operational support needs.
Develop and implement a clear, formal prioritization matrix for all Strategy Department activities, ensuring that critical strategic initiatives are adequately resourced and protected from ad-hoc diversions.
Review and, if necessary, augment the Strategy Department's staffing levels or reallocate non-strategic tasks to other relevant departments to ensure sufficient dedicated resources for core strategic functions.
Implement a robust project management tool or system to track strategic initiatives, monitor progress, identify bottlenecks early, and facilitate effective resource allocation and timeline adjustments.

observations.risk: Without a robust and consistently applied assessment framework, CREDICORP faces the risk of approving initiatives or launching products that are not financially viable, expose the Corporation to unquantified or excessive credit and operational risks, lead to regulatory non-compliance, or erode market share and reputation due to poorly conceived offerings. This could result in significant financial losses, misallocation of scarce resources, and failure to achieve strategic objectives, directly contravening the Corporation's risk appetite.
observations.title: Inadequate Assessment Framework for New Strategic Initiatives

updates.text: We are currently addressing the development of a comprehensive SOP for evaluating new strategic initiatives and product opportunities, including the creation of a standardized assessment template/checklist and a review and approval matrix. Initial milestones include completion of the SOP and template drafts, stakeholder review and validation, finalization of the approval matrix, and preparation for mandatory training and rollout across the Strategy Department.

observations.criteria: CREDICORP's Strategic Planning and Product Development Policy (Ref. SPDP/2023/001), Section 3.2, mandates that all new strategic initiatives and product options undergo a rigorous assessment process including documented market research, financial projections, operational impact analysis, and a comprehensive risk assessment (credit, operational, compliance, reputational) before submission to the Executive Management Committee (ExCo) or Board for approval.
observations.rootCause:
Lack of a clearly defined and communicated standard operating procedure (SOP) for the comprehensive assessment of new strategic initiatives and product options.
Insufficient training for Strategy Department personnel on the multi-faceted requirements for strategic initiative evaluation.
Absence of a dedicated tool or template to ensure all mandatory assessment components are consistently addressed and documented.
observations.description: The audit observed that several strategic initiatives and potential new product options, recently proposed or under consideration by the Strategy Department, lacked documented evidence of comprehensive risk assessments, market analyses, and financial viability studies prior to their presentation for executive approval. Specifically, proposals for 'CREDICORP Green Loan' and 'Digital Micro-Credit' facilities reviewed did not contain detailed impact analyses on existing portfolio performance, compliance implications, or comprehensive competitive landscape assessments, indicating a gap in the due diligence process for strategic decision-making.
observations.ownerResponse: The recommendation has been fully implemented. observations.description:

1. Non-Compliance with Existing Collateral Requirements: For certain PFIs (e.g., Optimus Bank), only a Direct Debit Mandate (DDM) was obtained as collateral, contrary to internal policy requiring a combination of collateral types.

2. Ambiguity in Collateral Policy Framework: The credit policy for Tier 2 banks does not specify how multiple collateral types should be combined or how to assess their sufficiency. For example, in a case where a PFI has both a Direct Debit Mandate (DDM) and T-bills, there is no guidance on whether the T-bills adequately cover the exposure or how to combine with other collaterals. This ambiguity increases the risk of under-collateralized loans and inconsistent application of credit risk mitigation.
observations.recommendation:

Review all PFI loans assess whether collateral coverage is sufficient relative to exposure and obtain additional collateral where feasible.

Develop a collateral adequacy calculation methodology or scoring system.
observations.managementResponse:
Credit Operations Department will develop and issue a Collateral Management Policy to provide clearer guidance on:

The methodology for assessing collateral adequacy.

Treatment and combination of multiple collateral types (e.g., DDM, Treasury Bills, guarantees).

Management will continue to ensure that all approved collateral structures are clearly documented in credit memos and monitored through the existing collateral register.

observations.title: Non-Compliance with Payment Documentation Requirements
observations.criteria: The Corporation's Financial Control Policy, Section 3.2.1 – Payment Processing, explicitly states that "all payments must be supported by complete, accurate, and duly authorized documentation, including but not limited to, approved invoices, purchase orders, delivery notes, service completion certificates, and payment requisition forms." This policy aims to ensure the legitimacy, accuracy, and proper authorization of all financial disbursements, adhering to principles of sound financial management and internal control.
observations.rootCause:
Inadequate adherence to established internal control procedures for payment processing within the Operations Department.
Lack of robust pre-payment verification checks by reviewing officers.
Insufficient training or awareness among Operations Department staff regarding the critical importance and specific requirements for complete documentation for all payments.
Potential pressure to expedite payments without completing all necessary compliance steps.
observations.description: During the audit of payment processes within the Operations Department for the period Q1 2024, it was observed that 15 out of 50 sampled payment transactions (30%) totaling approximately NGN 15,500,000 were processed and disbursed without complete and relevant supporting documents. Specifically, payments for vendor services and operational expenses lacked critical attachments such as approved invoices, service completion certificates, delivery notes, or duly authorized request forms. For instance, payment batch P_20240315_001 for NGN 2,500,000 to Vendor X for "consultancy services" did not include a signed contract or a service delivery report, making it impossible to verify the legitimacy and completion of the service rendered.
observations.recommendation:
Implement mandatory pre-payment checklists for all payment processors and approvers within the Operations Department to ensure all required supporting documents are attached and verified before payment approval.
Conduct refresher training for all staff involved in the payment process, emphasizing CREDICORP's Financial Control Policy, the specific documentation requirements, and the importance of complete documentation for all payments.
Strengthen supervisory review of payment batches, ensuring strict compliance with documentation requirements before final authorization.
Establish a clear escalation process for instances where documentation is incomplete, mandating resolution and proper authorization before payment is processed.
Consider implementing automated controls within the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system to prevent payment processing without required document uploads or digital approvals.

observations.title: Inadequate Funding for Strategic Sustainability Operations

updates.text:
Management has commenced actions to address this recommendation. A proposal for the establishment of a dedicated Sustainability Fund is currently being developed in collaboration with the Finance Department and will be incorporated into the annual budgeting process to ensure funding for approved sustainability initiatives is ring-fenced and protected from reallocation.

In addition, the Strategy and Finance Departments have initiated a review of existing and planned sustainability projects to determine funding requirements, develop realistic cost estimates, and identify potential funding gaps. A structured budgeting and financial monitoring framework, including budget tracking, variance analysis, and escalation procedures, is also being designed to strengthen financial oversight of sustainability initiatives.

Quarterly performance and financial review sessions for critical sustainability projects will be incorporated into Executive Management and Board committee reporting processes. The comprehensive funding assessment and implementation framework are expected to be finalized within the next budgeting cycle, with ongoing monitoring thereafter to ensure sustainable funding and effective project delivery.

Significant progress has been made towards implementing the recommendation. The Strategy and Finance Departments have commenced collaborative engagements to define the governance structure and funding requirements for a dedicated Sustainability Fund. A comprehensive review of all approved sustainability initiatives is currently underway to assess short-, medium-, and long-term funding requirements, validate cost estimates, and identify potential funding gaps. In parallel, a draft budgeting and financial management framework has been developed, covering budget planning, expenditure tracking, variance monitoring, and escalation procedures for funding shortfalls.

Management has also initiated the integration of sustainability project performance and financial reporting into existing governance forums, with quarterly review mechanisms being established for Executive Management and the relevant Board Committees. The detailed funding assessment and implementation roadmap are expected to be finalized during the current budget planning cycle, after which full implementation and ongoing monitoring will commence.

Management acknowledges the recommendation and has taken steps to strengthen the funding and governance framework for sustainability initiatives. A dedicated budget line for strategic sustainability projects has been incorporated into the budgeting process to improve funding visibility and resource allocation. Collaboration between the Strategy and Finance Departments has also been enhanced to ensure sustainability initiatives are supported by realistic financial projections and appropriate contingency provisions.

In addition, a structured project financial monitoring process, including periodic budget reviews and variance tracking, has been introduced to facilitate early identification and resolution of funding challenges. Sustainability projects will be presented during periodic management and Board reviews to ensure adequate oversight and timely decision-making. Furthermore, a comprehensive assessment of current and future funding requirements for sustainability initiatives is being conducted to support long-term planning and ensure alignment with the Corporation's strategic objectives.

These measures are expected to improve funding adequacy, project execution, and the overall sustainability of approved initiatives. The recommendation is hereby closed.

observations.criteria: CREDICORP's Strategic Plan 2024-2028 clearly articulates a strong commitment to ESG principles, setting specific, measurable targets for sustainability performance. The Corporation's approved annual operating budget and the Financial Management Policy (Section X) mandate that all approved strategic initiatives, particularly those with significant reputational and long-term business implications, must be adequately resourced and funded to ensure successful implementation and achievement of corporate objectives. Furthermore, industry best practices for corporate governance and sustainability reporting require demonstrable progress on stated ESG commitments.
observations.rootCause:
Inadequate initial financial assessment and realistic budgeting for complex, multi-year sustainability projects during the annual planning cycle.
Lack of a robust, ring-fenced funding mechanism or dedicated budget line item specifically for long-term strategic sustainability initiatives, making them vulnerable to re-allocation during periods of budget pressure.
Insufficient collaboration and clear communication channels between the Strategy Department and the Finance Department to ensure strategic priorities are fully understood and adequately resourced throughout the budget execution phase.
Absence of a formal process for periodic review and adjustment of sustainability project budgets to account for unforeseen economic fluctuations or evolving project requirements.
observations.closureNote: Remediation verified includes the establishment of a dedicated sustainability budget provision, implementation of a collaborative budgeting framework between Strategy and Finance, and strengthened project financial monitoring with executive reporting. Evidence reviewed included approved budget documentation, updated procedural guidelines, and confirmation of reporting to Executive Management and the Board Audit Committee. The recommendation is considered substantially addressed, with ongoing actions for future funding alignment integrated into strategic planning processes.
observations.description: During the audit of the Strategy Department's Sustainability Operations for the fiscal year 2023/2024, it was observed that several approved strategic sustainability initiatives, vital for achieving CREDICORP's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) goals, have experienced significant delays, scope reductions, or complete suspension due to a consistent and substantial shortfall in allocated funds. Specifically, projects such as the phased implementation of carbon footprint reduction measures across operations and the expansion of financial literacy outreach programmes in underserved communities have been hampered. Our review of project budgets versus actual expenditure revealed a cumulative funding gap of approximately NGN 750 million for critical sustainability projects planned for the current operating year, preventing their timely and effective execution as envisioned in the corporate strategy.
observations.agreedTarget: Implement revised budgeting procedures and establish a dedicated Sustainability Fund within 60 days; complete the re-evaluation of funding requirements for current initiatives within 90 days.
observations.ownerResponse:
Management has implemented the recommendation through a series of governance, budgeting, and financial oversight measures designed to strengthen the funding and sustainability of strategic initiatives.

A dedicated budget provision for sustainability and strategic initiatives has been established within the Corporation's approved annual budget and is maintained as a separate budget line under the Strategy Department's cost centre. Allocations under this provision are tracked independently and are protected from routine reallocation. Any proposed reallocation of funds from the provision is subject to the Corporation's approved Budget Variation and Virement Procedure and requires the approval of Executive Management, thereby ensuring that funds earmarked for sustainability initiatives remain ring-fenced and used only for their intended purpose.

In addition, a formal collaborative budgeting process between the Strategy and Finance Departments has been institutionalised as part of the annual planning and budget cycle. Under this process, all sustainability initiatives are jointly reviewed and assessed before budget approval, with detailed costing, implementation timelines, funding-source identification, risk assessments, and contingency requirements incorporated into the budgeting process. This ensures that approved initiatives are supported by realistic and adequately evaluated financial projections.

To improve project financial management, sustainability initiatives are now monitored through the Corporation's budget performance monitoring framework, which provides periodic budget utilisation reports and variance analysis against approved allocations. Where a funding shortfall or significant budget variance is identified, the issue is escalated through the responsible budget holder to Executive Management for resolution through funding reallocation, supplementary budget approval, or project reprioritisation, as applicable.

Quarterly performance and financial reviews of strategic sustainability initiatives have also been incorporated into Executive Management oversight processes. Project implementation status, budget utilisation, key risks, and funding gaps are reviewed by the Executive Management Committee, while material funding and performance issues are escalated to the Board Audit Committee through the Corporation's established governance and reporting framework.

Furthermore, a comprehensive review of current and projected funding requirements for approved sustainability initiatives over the next three to five years has been completed as part of the Corporation's strategic planning process. The outcome of this review has been incorporated into the Corporation's Medium-Term Strategic and Financial Plan and reflected in subsequent budget projections to ensure adequate funding for priority sustainability initiatives over the planning horizon.

Based on the actions completed above, Management considers the recommendation fully implemented and requests its closure.
observations.recommendation:
Establish a dedicated and ring-fenced Sustainability Fund within CREDICORP's annual budget, with specific allocations for approved strategic initiatives, ensuring resources are protected from re-allocation.
Implement a comprehensive and collaborative budgeting framework between the Strategy Department and Finance Department, ensuring all sustainability initiatives undergo rigorous financial planning, including realistic cost projections and contingency planning.
Develop and implement a robust project financial management system for sustainability initiatives, incorporating detailed budget tracking, regular variance analysis, and clear escalation procedures for funding shortfalls.
Mandate quarterly performance and financial reviews for all critical sustainability projects by the Executive Management Committee and the Board Audit Committee, ensuring timely identification and resolution of funding gaps.
Conduct a thorough re-evaluation of the current and projected funding requirements for all approved sustainability initiatives for the next 3-5 years, and adjust the Corporation's strategic financial plan accordingly.
