This rule has processed 61.61 GB of traffic with no application visibility or URL filtering in place.
observations.recommendation:
1. Replace the single any-to-any rule with specific rules for defined business functions (e.g., web browsing, email, payment systems).
2. Implement Web Filtering to block malicious and non-business-appropriate sites.
3.Implement Application Control to prevent unauthorised application traffic.
4.Separate the internal network into zones: User, Server, and Management VLANs.
5.Apply least-privilege principles: each zone should only be permitted the traffic necessary for its specific function.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS & Internal

The current firewall configuration reflects the organisation�s existing flat network architecture and was implemented to maintain operational continuity.

The development and approval of the relevant network security policies and standards will be prioritised to enable the implementation of appropriate firewall rules and segmentation.

Timeline: 10 April 2026

observations.risk: With an active brute-force campaign of over 51,000 attempts underway, the strength of the admin password is a critical line of defence. A weak or short password is far more likely to be guessed, especially in a distributed attack from 108 IP addresses. Without password expiry, a compromised password would remain valid indefinitely. This gap directly compounds the risk from Finding 1 (exposed management interface) and Finding 2 (no MFA).
observations.title: Password Policy Disabled � No Complexity, Length, or Expiry Requirements
observations.rootCause: System Settings (Appendix 5): Password scope = 'Off'. No minimum length, complexity, or expiry enforced for any admin account. super_admin 'admin' account therefore protected only by password of unknown strength.
observations.description: The firewall's built-in password policy is turned off. There are no enforced requirements for minimum password length, complexity (e.g., mix of uppercase, numbers, and symbols), or expiration for any administrator account. The highest-privilege account on the device could theoretically have a very short or simple password with no technical control preventing this.
observations.recommendation:
1. Enable the Password Policy: System > Settings > Password Policy � set scope to 'Both'.
2. Set minimum password length to 12 characters.
3. Require complexity: uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The firewall password policy will be configured and enforced immediately to ensure appropriate password complexity, minimum length, and other relevant security requirements.

Timeline: 1 week

observations.risk: Any network monitoring tool or attacker positioned on the same network path can capture and read all Telnet traffic in real time � including admin credentials. On a firewall that is already under active brute-force attack, exposing any plaintext authentication channel is unacceptable. Telnet has no legitimate modern use case on a security device when SSH is available.
observations.title: Telnet Administrative Service Configured � Unencrypted Management Protocol
observations.rootCause: Telnet configured as administrative service on the FortiGate. Telnet transmits all data including credentials in unencrypted plaintext over the network. No legitimate use case on a production security device when SSH is available.
observations.description: Telnet is configured as an available administrative service on the firewall. Telnet is an obsolete protocol that transmits all communication � including usernames, passwords, and all commands � in plain, unencrypted text across the network. It was superseded by SSH (Secure Shell) over 25 years ago and should not be present on any production security device.
observations.recommendation:
1. Disable Telnet immediately via CLI: config system global > set admin-telnet disable > end.
2. Verify that SSH (port 22) remains enabled as the sole CLI management protocol.
3. Restrict SSH access to trusted management IP addresses only, consistent with Finding 1 recommendations.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

Telnet is recognised as an insecure and obsolete protocol. Telnet will be disabled immediately, and administrative access will be restricted to secure, encrypted protocols in line with security best practices.

Timeline: 1 week

observations.risk: Every security event in this firewall's history has the wrong time recorded. For the potential incident identified in Finding 2, configuration changes logged as occurring in the middle of the night are actually mid-morning business hours � a material difference for investigation purposes. In any regulatory investigation, forensic analysis, or legal proceeding, incorrect timestamps undermine the evidential value of the logs. PCI DSS explicitly requires all system clocks to be correctly synchronised.
observations.title: System Timezone Set to Pacific Time � 9-Hour Log Timestamp Error
observations.rootCause: System Settings (Appendix 7): Timezone = GMT-8:00 (Pacific Time, US & Canada). CREDICORP operates in Nigeria under WAT (UTC+1). All 52,816 log entries carry tz='-0700'. Actual WAT time = displayed time + 9 hours.
observations.description: The firewall's system clock is set to GMT-8 (Pacific Time, USA) instead of West Africa Time (WAT, UTC+1), which is the correct timezone for CREDICORP's operations in Nigeria. This means every single log entry on this device has a timestamp that is 9 hours behind actual local time. All 52,816 log entries analysed in this audit carry this incorrect timestamp.
observations.recommendation:
1. Immediately correct the timezone: System > Settings > Time zone > Africa/Lagos (UTC+1/WAT).
2. Verify NTP synchronisation continues to function correctly after the timezone correction.
3. Document the affected log period in all audit and incident records � all historical logs must have 9 hours added to show the true local time.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

Management acknowledges the observation. The firewall�s system clock will be corrected to West Africa Time (WAT, UTC+1) to ensure that all log entries accurately reflect local time.

observations.risk: Anyone with physical access to the firewall � a cleaning contractor, a disgruntled employee, a courier � could insert a pre-prepared USB drive and completely overwrite the firewall's configuration or firmware in seconds, with no credentials required and potentially no audit trail. For a financial institution's perimeter firewall, this is an unacceptable physical security bypass of all digital access controls. This risk is elevated given the suspected unauthorised access identified in Finding 2.
observations.title: USB Auto-Install Enabled � Unauthenticated Physical Override
observations.rootCause: System Settings (Appendix 8): USB auto-install enabled for 'Detect configuration' (fgt_system.conf) and 'Detect firmware' (image.out). Insertion of USB containing these filenames applies config/firmware automatically with no GUI/CLI authentication required.
observations.description: The firewall is configured to automatically apply any configuration file or firmware image found on a USB drive inserted into the device � with no password, no MFA, and no administrator approval required. This feature is intended for initial factory deployment of new devices but has not been disabled now that the device is in live production.
observations.recommendation:
1. Disable USB auto-install immediately: System > Settings > Start Up Settings � set both 'Detect configuration' and 'Detect firmware' toggles to OFF.
2. Review and enforce physical access controls to the network cabinet or server room housing the FortiGate, including access logs and CCTV coverage.
3. Use authenticated methods (FortiManager or TFTP/SCP) for all firmware and configuration management.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The automatic USB-based configuration and firmware update feature will be disabled immediately to prevent unauthorized changes

observations.risk: Without traffic logging, CREDICORP cannot determine what data has left the network, which internal devices have made suspicious connections, or whether any malware is communicating with external attacker-controlled servers. In the context of the potential compromise in Finding 2, it is impossible to determine from current logs whether any data was stolen. Without external log forwarding, an attacker who gains firewall access can erase all evidence of their activity.
observations.title: Incomplete Local Traffic Logging and No External Syslog Forwarding
observations.rootCause: Log & Report Global Settings (Appendix 9): Log allowed traffic = OFF; Log denied unicast = OFF; Log denied broadcast = OFF; Log local out traffic = ON only. Syslog status = Disabled. Event logging = 'All' (source of brute-force and admin event logs analysed in this report). 61.61 GB outbound traffic from Lan_To_Internet has zero session-level log record.
observations.description:
Incomplete Local Traffic Logging and No External Syslog Forwarding
The firewall is not logging allowed or denied network traffic passing through it � only system events (like login attempts) are being recorded. Additionally, no logs are being forwarded to any external system: if the firewall's local log storage is cleared or the device is compromised, all evidence of what occurred is permanently lost. The 61.61 GB of outbound traffic processed has no destination or content record anywhere.
observations.recommendation:
1. Enable 'Log allowed traffic' and 'Log denied unicast traffic' in Log & Report > Global Settings > Local Traffic Logging.
2. Configure Syslog forwarding to an external, dedicated log management server or SIEM solution (e.g., FortiAnalyzer, Splunk, or any RFC 5424-compatible syslog receiver).
3. Set log retention: minimum 90 days online, 12 months archived, per PCI DSS Req. 10.7.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The limited logging is currently due to storage constraints on the firewall. While full logging and forwarding to a centralized security information system (CIS) could be implemented, the immediate cost-benefit may not justify it given the current network architecture.

As an interim measure, a rotational logging mechanism will be explored to capture critical network traffic until a centralized logging solution can be implemented in line with best practices.

Timeline: 10 April 2026

observations.risk: For a financial institution, the firewall is the gateway for payment processing, customer-facing systems, VPN access for remote staff, and email. A single hardware failure causes a complete outage of all these services with no automatic recovery. The ongoing active attack campaign also increases the risk of availability impact from resource exhaustion. This is both a business continuity risk and, for a regulated institution, a potential compliance gap.
observations.title: No High Availability � Firewall is a Single Point of Failure
observations.rootCause: HA settings (Appenndix 10): Mode = Standalone. No cluster partner configured. Device sustaining 2,986 concurrent sessions and active attack campaign � operating under load with no redundancy.
observations.description:
No High Availability � Firewall is a Single Point of Failure
The firewall is operating in 'Standalone' mode with no backup unit configured. There is no automatic failover capability. If this firewall fails � due to hardware fault, power loss, software crash, or even a routine firmware upgrade � all internet-dependent services stop immediately until manual intervention restores the device.
observations.recommendation:
1. Formally document the single-point-of-failure risk and obtain management sign-off if HA cannot be implemented immediately.
2. Evaluate deploying a second FortiGate 60F in Active-Passive HA mode for automatic failover.
3. At minimum: maintain a current, tested configuration backup stored off-device, and document a hardware replacement procedure with a defined Recovery Time Objective (RTO).
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

Given the current scale of operations, this level of redundancy is considered acceptable.

Management will reassess the need for high-availability and failover capabilities as operational requirements and service dependencies increase.

Timeline: 10 April 2026

observations.risk: A security device with undetected file system corruption may load its configuration incorrectly, have security profiles fail silently, or produce unreliable log files � all without alerting administrators. In the context of the suspected unauthorised access in Finding 2, file system integrity verification is particularly important, as a sophisticated attacker may attempt to modify system files. Silent degradation of a security device is especially dangerous.
observations.title: Auto File System Check Disabled � Silent Corruption Risk
observations.rootCause: System Settings (Appendix 8): 'Auto file system check' toggled OFF. Feature performs FortiOS file system integrity validation at boot time, detecting and correcting errors before system online.
observations.description: A built-in safety feature that checks the firewall's internal file system for errors at startup is turned off. This check is designed to detect and correct file system problems � caused by unexpected power-offs, hardware degradation, or deliberate tampering � before the device comes back online. Without it, file system errors could persist undetected.
observations.recommendation:
1. Enable Auto File System Check: System > Settings > Start Up Settings � toggle 'Auto file system check' to ON.
2. Combine with regular firmware integrity checks and configuration backup verification.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The firewall�s built-in file system integrity check will be re-enabled.

observations.risk: The continued understaffing significantly jeopardizes CREDICORP's ability to innovate and maintain a competitive edge in the rapidly evolving consumer credit market. This could lead to a loss of market share, diminished customer satisfaction due to delayed or substandard product launches, and reputational damage as competitors introduce more advanced solutions. Moreover, the strain on existing staff can lead to burnout, increased attrition, and a higher risk of errors in product development and implementation, potentially exposing the Corporation to operational and financial risks.
observations.title: Insufficient Staffing Levels within Innovation Department
observations.criteria: CREDICORP's Human Resources Policy (Section 3.1) stipulates that departments must maintain adequate staffing levels to meet operational demands and strategic objectives. Furthermore, the Innovation Department's annual operating plan (2024) and project charters for strategic initiatives (e.g., 'Project Falcon' and 'Project Phoenix') outline specific resource requirements necessary for timely delivery and high-quality output.
observations.rootCause:
Lack of a robust, forward-looking workforce planning strategy specifically tailored to the specialized and evolving needs of the Innovation Department.
Protracted and inefficient recruitment processes for specialized innovation roles, leading to extended vacancy periods.
Insufficient budget allocation for competitive compensation packages, making it challenging to attract and retain high-calibre talent in a competitive market.
observations.description: The Innovation Department is operating with significant staffing shortages across critical functions. Specifically, observations revealed a deficit in Product Development Specialists, Data Scientists, and UI/UX Designers, with 30% of key innovation-related positions currently vacant for an average of six months. This has resulted in a 45% delay in the projected timelines for the launch of two strategic digital credit products and a 25% reduction in the department's capacity to engage in new research and development initiatives for the current quarter.
observations.recommendation:
Conduct an urgent and comprehensive workforce planning and skills gap analysis for the Innovation Department, projecting staffing needs for the next 12-24 months based on CREDICORP's strategic innovation roadmap.
Streamline and accelerate the recruitment and onboarding process for critical innovation roles, potentially leveraging specialized external recruitment agencies or internal fast-track hiring protocols for high-priority positions.
Review and adjust the compensation and benefits structure for specialized innovation roles to ensure competitiveness within the industry, thereby enhancing talent attraction and retention.
Develop and implement a talent development and retention program, including continuous training, career progression paths, and mentorship, to foster internal growth and reduce attrition.

tor.addressee: Head Procurement, Head Risk Management, Head Credit Portfolio, Head Finance
tor.background:
Background and Purpose

This review forms part of the approved risk-based Annual Internal Audit Plan for 2026 and is being conducted in line with the Corporation's drive to improve productivity, reduce cost-to-income and enhance service delivery across its core functions. As CREDICORP scales its lending operations, the efficiency of the processes that support the business — the Credit Portfolio origination-to-collection lifecycle, Procurement (procure-to-pay), Finance (financial close, payments and reporting) and Risk Management — has a direct bearing on customer experience, operating cost and the timeliness of management decision-making. Unlike a conventional controls-assurance review, this audit looks specifically at the economy, efficiency and effectiveness (value-for-money) of these processes, covering the period 1 April to 30 June 2026 (Q2 2026).

The purpose of the audit is to assess how efficiently these four functions operate — examining cycle times and turnaround, levels of manual effort and automation, handoffs and bottlenecks, rework and error rates, duplication of activity, resource utilisation and the management of SLAs/KPIs — and to identify practical, quantified opportunities to streamline, automate and improve without weakening control. On completion, Internal Audit will provide Management and the Board Audit Committee with independent assurance on the operational efficiency and process-improvement maturity of the four functions, together with prioritised, actionable recommendations. We count on the cooperation of process owners and staff in providing timely access to process data, systems and personnel, and we will agree all observations with you before finalising our report.

audits.area: Credit Portfolio, Procurement, Finance, Risk Management
audits.name: Operational Efficiency and Process Improvement Audit

plan.scope: This process audit assesses the operational efficiency and process-improvement maturity of four functions — Credit Portfolio (origination-to-collection lifecycle), Procurement (procure-to-pay), Finance (financial close, payments and reporting) and Risk Management — for the period 1 April to 30 June 2026 (Q2 2026). It focuses on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness (value-for-money) of these processes: cycle times and turnaround, manual effort and automation levels, hand-offs and bottlenecks, rework and error rates, duplication of activity, resource utilisation, SLA/KPI performance, and the extent to which continuous-improvement and data analytics are embedded. It evaluates whether controls are efficient (not just effective) and whether process design supports the Corporation's cost-to-income and service objectives. It does NOT re-perform a full controls-assurance/compliance audit of each function (those are covered by separate risk-based reviews), nor does it cover credit-decision quality, IT general controls, HR/payroll, or strategy formulation, except where these directly affect process efficiency. Absent restriction, the review covers Q2 2026 transactional throughput and process data across the four functions.

tests.title: End-to-end cycle-time and SLA analysis
tests.objective: Confirm whether core processes complete within defined cycle times/SLAs and identify delays and bottlenecks.
tests.procedure: For each function, obtain transaction timestamp data for Q2 2026 (loan application-to-disbursement; requisition-to-PO-to-payment; period-end close timeline; risk-report production cycle). Compute actual cycle times and stage durations, compare to defined SLAs/targets, and identify the slowest stages, outliers and queues. Map where time is lost and quantify backlog/ageing.
tests.population: All in-scope transactions/processes with start–end timestamps in Q2 2026 across the four functions.
tests.sampleBasis: 100% data analytics on cycle times where timestamp data exists; judgemental deep-dive on the slowest decile and aged/backlog items.
tests.controlTested: Process efficiency and SLA performance (timeliness/efficiency).

tests.title: Process mapping and bottleneck / non-value-add identification
tests.objective: Identify bottlenecks, non-value-adding steps, and unclear ownership in each end-to-end process.
tests.procedure: Develop or validate end-to-end process maps (narrative/flowchart) for a key process in each function. Apply lean analysis to classify each step as value-add, business-non-value-add, or waste. Identify bottlenecks, redundant approvals, wait states, and steps lacking clear ownership. Corroborate via walkthroughs and staff interviews.
tests.population: Documented and observed process flows for selected core processes in each function.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental — one high-volume/high-impact process per function, mapped end-to-end.
tests.controlTested: Process design efficiency and ownership clarity (effectiveness/efficiency).

tests.title: Automation and straight-through-processing assessment
tests.objective: Assess the level of automation/STP and identify manual, spreadsheet and re-keying effort that could be automated.
tests.procedure: For each function, inventory the systems used and identify steps performed manually, in spreadsheets, or on paper, and points where the same data is re-keyed across systems. Quantify manual effort (volume × time) and STP rates. Benchmark against available system capability and identify candidate automations (system config, RPA, integration).
tests.population: Process-step inventory and system landscape for the four functions in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Full process-step inventory per selected process; judgemental quantification of the highest-effort manual tasks.
tests.controlTested: Degree of automation and elimination of manual effort (efficiency).

tests.title: Rework, error and exception analysis
tests.objective: Quantify rework, errors and exceptions and determine their root causes and efficiency cost.
tests.procedure: Extract exception/rejection/rework data for Q2 2026 (e.g. returned requisitions, failed three-way matches, mis-booked loans, reconciliation differences, re-run/restated reports). Calculate error/rework rates by process and team, perform root-cause analysis on the largest categories, and estimate rework effort/cost. Identify recurring, avoidable causes.
tests.population: Exception, rejection, error and rework logs across the four functions for Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: 100% analytics on available exception data; judgemental root-cause sampling of top error categories.
tests.controlTested: First-time-right / rework rate (quality/efficiency).

tests.title: Handoff and cross-functional friction review
tests.objective: Confirm handoffs between Credit, Procurement, Finance and Risk are timely, clear and free of duplication.
tests.procedure: Map key inter-function handoffs (e.g. credit disbursement-to-finance posting; procurement-to-AP/finance; risk data-to-credit and risk-to-finance reporting). For a sample, measure handoff lag, identify data re-entry, reconciliation breaks and disputes over ownership, and assess SLAs between functions. Interview both sides of each handoff.
tests.population: Inter-function handoff transactions and interfaces in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental sample of the principal handoffs between each pair of functions, with timing analysis.
tests.controlTested: Efficiency and clarity of cross-functional handoffs (process integration).

tests.title: KPI/SLA framework and performance reporting review
tests.objective: Confirm meaningful efficiency KPIs/SLAs exist, are measured, reported and acted upon.
tests.procedure: Obtain the KPI/SLA definitions and performance reports for each function for Q2 2026. Assess whether metrics cover efficiency (cycle time, cost, throughput, error/rework, backlog), are accurately measured, regularly reported to management, and drive corrective action. Recompute selected KPIs from source data to verify reliability.
tests.population: KPI/SLA definitions, dashboards and management reports for the four functions, Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Full review of the KPI suite per function; recomputation of a sample of reported metrics.
tests.controlTested: Performance measurement and management of efficiency (monitoring).

tests.title: Resource utilisation and capacity analysis
tests.objective: Assess whether staff and processing capacity are efficiently deployed relative to workload.
tests.procedure: Compare workload volumes to headcount/effort across teams in the four functions for Q2 2026. Identify imbalances — overtime, backlogs, idle capacity, key-person dependencies. Compute productivity ratios (transactions per FTE, cost per transaction) and benchmark across teams/periods. Review use of temporary/overtime resourcing.
tests.population: Workload volumes, staffing/effort and overtime data for the four functions in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Analytical review across all in-scope teams; judgemental focus on teams with backlog or high overtime.
tests.controlTested: Efficient deployment of resources (economy/efficiency).

tests.title: Control efficiency / duplication review
tests.objective: Identify duplicated, redundant or disproportionately costly controls that can be streamlined without raising risk.
tests.procedure: Inventory key controls in the selected processes (approvals, reconciliations, checks, reports). Identify overlapping or repeated controls across steps/functions, multiple sign-offs adding little risk reduction, and reconciliations performed in more than one place. Assess each for risk-proportionality and recommend rationalisation while preserving control objectives.
tests.population: Key-control inventory for the selected processes across the four functions.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental review of the key controls in each mapped process.
tests.controlTested: Efficiency and proportionality of controls (control rationalisation).

tests.title: Process documentation (SOP) currency and adherence
tests.objective: Confirm processes are supported by current, approved SOPs and executed consistently.
tests.procedure: For each function, confirm SOPs exist, are approved and current, and reflect the actual process. Walk through a sample of transactions against the SOP to test adherence and identify undocumented workarounds. Note where outdated documentation drives inefficiency, inconsistency or training overhead.
tests.population: SOPs and a sample of executed transactions for the four functions.
tests.sampleBasis: Full review of relevant SOPs; judgemental walkthrough sample per process.
tests.controlTested: Standardisation and documentation supporting efficient execution (consistency).

tests.title: Continuous-improvement and analytics maturity assessment
tests.objective: Assess whether functions actively identify, prioritise and implement process improvements using data.
tests.procedure: Review evidence of continuous-improvement activity in Q2 2026 — improvement registers, automation initiatives, post-incident/root-cause actions, and use of data analytics/dashboards. Assess governance over improvement (ownership, tracking to closure) and whether prior identified inefficiencies were addressed. Benchmark maturity against good practice.
tests.population: Improvement registers, automation/initiative records and analytics outputs for the four functions.
tests.sampleBasis: Full review of available improvement records; judgemental assessment of closure of prior inefficiencies.
tests.controlTested: Continuous-improvement and data-driven management maturity (effectiveness).

tests.title: Cost-of-process / value-for-money analysis
tests.objective: Estimate the cost of running each process and identify value-for-money improvement opportunities.
tests.procedure: For a selected process per function, estimate the cost to process (effort, system, rework and delay costs) and unit cost per transaction. Compare across functions/periods and against the value delivered. Quantify the savings potential of the improvement opportunities identified in T2–T8 and prioritise by impact and ease of implementation.
tests.population: Cost, volume and effort data for the selected processes in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental — one representative high-volume process per function, costed end-to-end.
tests.controlTested: Economy and value for money of processes (cost efficiency).

keyRisks: Excessive end-to-end cycle times (e.g. loan processing, PO-to-payment, financial close, risk reporting) reducing service quality, competitiveness and timely decision-making.
Heavy reliance on manual, spreadsheet-based and paper processes with low straight-through processing, increasing cost, error and key-person dependency.
Bottlenecks and unclear ownership at handoffs between Credit, Procurement, Finance and Risk causing delay, backlog and duplicated effort.
High rework, exception and error rates (e.g. rejected requisitions, mis-keyed loans, reconciliation differences, re-run risk reports) consuming capacity and inflating cost.
Duplication of activity and controls across functions (e.g. multiple re-keying of the same data, overlapping reconciliations and reports) adding cost without added assurance.
Absence or non-use of meaningful SLAs/KPIs and process metrics, so inefficiency and backlogs go unmeasured and unmanaged.
Sub-optimal resource utilisation — uneven workload distribution, overtime/backlogs in some teams and under-utilisation in others.
Inefficient or redundant controls that slow processing without commensurate risk reduction.
Outdated, missing or unfollowed process documentation (SOPs) leading to inconsistent execution and onboarding inefficiency.
Weak continuous-improvement culture and limited use of data analytics/automation, so known inefficiencies persist.
Slow risk and management reporting (manual data aggregation) delaying decisions and increasing the cost of assurance.
objectives: Assess whether key processes in Credit Portfolio, Procurement, Finance and Risk Management operate efficiently — within defined cycle times/SLAs and without avoidable delay, bottlenecks or backlog.
Evaluate the level of manual effort, automation and straight-through processing, and identify opportunities to streamline, automate or eliminate non-value-adding and duplicated activities.
Determine the extent of rework, errors, exceptions and re-processing, and assess their root causes and cost.
Assess whether resources (people, systems, spend) are deployed efficiently relative to workload and output across the four functions.
Evaluate whether SLAs/KPIs are defined, measured, reported and actively managed, and whether continuous-improvement mechanisms and process documentation are embedded.
Confirm that handoffs and dependencies between the functions (e.g. credit-to-finance, procurement-to-finance, risk-to-credit) are clear, timely and not a source of friction or duplication.
Identify quantified, actionable process-improvement opportunities that enhance efficiency without weakening control.

plan.scope: This process audit covers CREDICORP's end-to-end Procure-to-Pay (P2P) cycle and staff expense management for the period 1 April to 30 June 2026 (Q2 2026). It covers vendor onboarding and master-data maintenance; purchase requisitioning and approval; sourcing/tendering and award; purchase order creation; goods/services receipt; invoice processing and three-way matching; staff expense claims and advances/retirements; payment authorisation and execution; and related general-ledger posting, accruals and reconciliations for the quarter. It also covers compliance with the procurement policy, delegation-of-authority and budgetary controls, and applicable regulatory/tax obligations (e.g. WHT/VAT, CBN/DFI procurement governance). It excludes capital project/major contract management beyond P2P transactional controls, payroll, treasury and bank-funding operations, fixed-asset accounting beyond procurement receipt, and IT general controls except where they directly affect P2P processing. Absent restriction, the review covers all material expense and procurement transactions processed in Q2 2026 across all departments and locations.

tests.title: Requisition and purchase authorisation within delegated authority and budget
tests.objective: Confirm purchases were requisitioned, approved within the delegation of authority, and within approved budget before commitment.
tests.procedure: From the population of POs/purchases raised in Q2 2026, select a sample. For each, verify an approved requisition exists with business justification, that approval was given at the correct authority level per the DoA matrix before the PO/commitment date, and that the spend was within available budget. Confirm the PO predates the invoice and goods receipt.
tests.population: All purchase requisitions/POs raised in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Risk-based judgemental/random sample (e.g. 30–40), stratified by value and department, including all high-value and emergency/sole-source purchases.
tests.controlTested: Authorisation and budgetary control over procurement (authorisation/occurrence).

tests.title: Competitive sourcing and award compliance
tests.objective: Confirm procurements followed competitive/sourcing requirements and that awards were justified and authorised.
tests.procedure: For a sample of awards, verify the required number of quotations/tenders was obtained, evaluation was performed and documented by a tender committee where applicable, and the award was approved. Review sole-source/emergency procurements for documented justification and independent approval. Test for bid-splitting by analysing multiple POs to the same vendor just below thresholds.
tests.population: All awards/POs in Q2 2026 and the vendor-spend transaction listing.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental sample of awards above threshold plus analytical scan of 100% of POs for split-purchase patterns.
tests.controlTested: Competitive procurement and award authorisation (compliance/anti bid-rigging).

tests.title: Vendor onboarding and master-data integrity
tests.objective: Confirm vendors are legitimate, properly onboarded, and the vendor master is free of duplicates/fictitious and related-party records.
tests.procedure: Review onboarding for a sample of vendors active in Q2 2026 (CAC, TIN, bank verification, due diligence). Analyse the full vendor master for duplicates (name/TIN/account/address), dormant accounts, and vendor bank accounts matching employee accounts. Screen vendor directors/ownership against employee/related-party data for undisclosed conflicts.
tests.population: Vendor master file and vendors transacted in Q2 2026; employee master for matching.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental sample of new/active vendors plus 100% analytical duplicate/employee-account matching.
tests.controlTested: Vendor legitimacy and master-data integrity (validity/completeness; anti ghost-vendor).

tests.title: Vendor bank-detail change control
tests.objective: Confirm changes to vendor bank details are independently verified and authorised under maker-checker.
tests.procedure: Extract vendor bank-detail change logs for Q2 2026. For a sample, confirm an independent, documented verification (e.g. callback to a known contact) and maker-checker authorisation occurred, supported by a valid request. Identify changes made shortly before a payment run and payments made immediately after a detail change.
tests.population: All vendor bank-detail change records in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Analytical review of the full change log with judgemental sampling of high-risk changes for authorisation testing.
tests.controlTested: Integrity and authorisation of vendor bank-detail changes (data integrity; anti-BEC/payment diversion).

tests.title: Goods/services receipt verification
tests.objective: Confirm goods/services were received, independently verified, and agree to the order before payment.
tests.procedure: For a sample of payments, trace to a goods/service receipt note (GRN) or service acceptance confirming quantity and specification, completed by someone independent of the requisitioner. Agree GRN to PO and invoice. For services, confirm evidence of delivery/acceptance. Test for invoices paid without a valid receipt.
tests.population: Goods/service receipts and paid invoices for Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental sample overlapping payment testing, weighted to high-value and service procurements.
tests.controlTested: Independent receipt/acceptance of goods and services (occurrence/accuracy).

tests.title: Invoice processing and three-way matching
tests.objective: Confirm invoices are accurately processed and subject to effective three-way matching and duplicate detection.
tests.procedure: For a sample of invoices, verify a three-way match (PO, GRN, invoice) on quantity, price and amount within tolerance, with exceptions approved. Recompute invoice totals, taxes and any discounts. Run analytics across the AP population for duplicate invoice numbers, amounts, and same-vendor same-amount/same-date payments.
tests.population: All vendor invoices processed in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental sample for match testing plus 100% analytical duplicate-invoice/amount scan.
tests.controlTested: Three-way matching and duplicate-invoice control (accuracy/completeness).

tests.title: Payment validity, authorisation and accuracy
tests.objective: Confirm payments are valid, correctly authorised, made to the correct payee, and not duplicated.
tests.procedure: From the Q2 2026 payment population, select a sample and trace each payment to an approved, matched invoice and the correct vendor bank account. Verify payment authorisation per the DoA and bank mandate, and that maker/checker were different. Review manual/emergency/urgent payments for justification and approval. Reconcile payments to bank statements and scan for duplicate payments.
tests.population: All payments/disbursements processed in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Risk-based sample including all high-value and manual/emergency payments plus 100% duplicate-payment analytics.
tests.controlTested: Payment authorisation, accuracy and validity (authorisation/occurrence; anti duplicate payment).

tests.title: Staff expense claims, advances and retirements
tests.objective: Confirm staff expenses and advances are valid, supported, within policy, approved, and retired on time.
tests.procedure: For a sample of expense claims and advances in Q2 2026, verify valid supporting receipts, business purpose, compliance with expense policy/rates, and approval at the appropriate level. Confirm advances were retired within the policy timeframe and outstanding/unretired advances are followed up. Test for duplicate or personal claims.
tests.population: All staff expense claims, advances and retirements in Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental/random sample stratified by claimant level and value, with review of all long-outstanding advances.
tests.controlTested: Validity and policy compliance of expenses/advances (occurrence/accuracy/compliance).

tests.title: Segregation of duties and P2P system access
tests.objective: Confirm no single user can perform conflicting P2P functions and that system access/authority limits are appropriate.
tests.procedure: Obtain P2P system roles/entitlements. Map users across vendor-master maintenance, requisition, approval, goods receipt and payment to identify SoD conflicts. Review users with the ability to both create a vendor and process payment, and those with override/threshold-change rights. Using logs, test a sample of transactions for different maker/checker. Test leavers for timely access removal.
tests.population: All P2P user entitlements and the Q2 2026 transaction log.
tests.sampleBasis: Full review of entitlements for conflicts; analytical scan of transactions for same-user conflicts with sample follow-up.
tests.controlTested: Segregation of duties and logical access over P2P (SoD/access control).

tests.title: Approval-threshold override and split-transaction analytics
tests.objective: Confirm approval thresholds and authority limits are enforced and not circumvented.
tests.procedure: Analyse Q2 2026 requisitions/POs/payments for transactions clustered just below approval thresholds, repeated splits to the same vendor, and use of override/emergency provisions. For a sample of overrides and threshold-edge transactions, confirm justification and senior approval. Review the DoA configuration in the system for accuracy.
tests.population: All requisitions, POs and payments in Q2 2026 and system override logs.
tests.sampleBasis: 100% analytical review for threshold-edge/split patterns; judgemental sample of flagged items and overrides.
tests.controlTested: Enforcement of authority limits and thresholds (authorisation/anti-override).

tests.title: Tax compliance (WHT/VAT) on procurement
tests.objective: Confirm withholding tax and VAT are correctly deducted, accounted for, and remitted on procurement transactions.
tests.procedure: For a sample of vendor payments, recompute WHT and VAT, confirm correct deduction and that VAT was charged by registered vendors. Verify remittance of WHT/VAT to the relevant authority within statutory timelines and that credit notes/receipts are obtained. Identify payments where required deductions were not made.
tests.population: Vendor payments and tax remittance records for Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental sample weighted to high-value and service contracts subject to WHT/VAT.
tests.controlTested: Tax compliance over procurement payments (compliance/accuracy).

tests.title: Expenditure recording, accruals and reconciliations
tests.objective: Confirm expenditure is completely and accurately recorded and that AP/accruals and reconciliations are valid for the quarter.
tests.procedure: For a sample of transactions, confirm correct GL account, cost centre, period and amount. Test cut-off around quarter-end for goods/invoices received not recorded (completeness) and amounts recorded early. Review AP and accrual reconciliations for Q2 2026 for preparation, independent review, and clearance of reconciling/aged items.
tests.population: P2P GL postings, AP ledger and accrual reconciliations for Q2 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgemental sample of postings plus full review of quarter-end reconciliations and cut-off testing around 30 June 2026.
tests.controlTested: Completeness, accuracy and cut-off of expenditure and reconciliation control (accuracy/completeness).

keyRisks: Purchases committed without approval, outside delegated authority, or over budget, resulting in unauthorised or wasteful expenditure.
Circumvention of competitive procurement through bid-splitting, inappropriate sole-sourcing, or split purchase orders kept just below approval thresholds.
Fictitious or duplicate (ghost) vendors, or undisclosed related-party/conflict-of-interest vendors, used to divert funds.
Unauthorised changes to vendor bank details (internal or via business-email-compromise) redirecting legitimate payments to fraudulent accounts.
Payment for goods/services not received, short-delivered, or substandard due to weak or non-independent goods-receipt controls.
Inflated, false, or duplicate invoices paid through failure of three-way matching and duplicate-invoice detection.
Duplicate, inaccurate, or unauthorised payments, including manual/emergency payments bypassing standard controls.
Kickbacks/bribery and favouritism in vendor selection and award (corruption risk).
Staff expense claims that are inflated, personal, unsupported, or duplicated, and advances not retired on a timely basis.
Inadequate segregation of duties or excessive system access allowing one person to create a vendor, raise a PO, approve and pay.
Non-deduction/non-remittance of WHT/VAT and inaccurate or incomplete recording of expenditure, accruals and GL postings.
Override or manipulation of approval thresholds and authority limits in the P2P system.
objectives: Determine whether purchases and expenses are properly requisitioned, competitively sourced where required, and authorised within the delegation of authority and approved budget before commitment.
Confirm that vendors are legitimate, properly onboarded and that vendor master data (including bank details) is controlled, accurate and free of duplicate or fictitious records.
Assess whether goods and services are received and verified before payment, and that invoices are accurately processed and subject to effective three-way matching.
Evaluate whether payments are valid, accurate, made to the correct payee, properly authorised, and not duplicated.
Determine whether staff expense claims, advances and retirements are valid, supported, within policy, and approved.
Assess segregation of duties across requisition, approval, vendor-master, receipt and payment, and the adequacy of system access.
Confirm compliance with procurement policy, tax/regulatory requirements (WHT/VAT), and accurate, complete recording of expenditure, accruals and reconciliations for the quarter.

plan.scope: The audit will assess CREDICORP's strategic planning framework, the alignment of operational activities with Q3 2026 strategic objectives, and the effectiveness of monitoring and reporting mechanisms for strategic performance. It will cover the period leading up to and including Q3 2026, focusing on strategy formulation, communication, execution, and oversight. The audit will not include a detailed financial audit of specific transactions or an in-depth review of credit product profitability unless directly impacting overall strategic objectives and their achievement.

tests.title: Strategic Framework & Board Oversight Review
tests.objective: Confirm the existence, completeness, and formal approval of CREDICORP's strategic planning framework and objectives.
tests.procedure: Obtain and review board-approved strategic plan documents (e.g., 2024-2027 Strategic Plan, Q3 2026 objectives), related policies, and minutes of Board/Strategy Committee meetings where strategy formulation and approval were discussed.
tests.population: Strategic planning documentation, Board/Strategy Committee minutes (last 12-18 months).
tests.sampleBasis: All relevant strategic plan documents and Board minutes from the last 12-18 months.
tests.controlTested: Effectiveness of formal strategic planning and oversight by the Board and senior management.

tests.title: Strategic Objective Cascade and Communication Assessment
tests.objective: Evaluate if strategic objectives are effectively communicated, understood, and cascaded into departmental work plans across relevant CREDICORP units.
tests.procedure: Review departmental operating plans and individual performance objectives for alignment with corporate strategic objectives. Conduct interviews with a sample of departmental heads and key personnel to assess understanding and implementation.
tests.population: Corporate strategic plan, departmental work plans, performance appraisal documents, key management personnel.
tests.sampleBasis: Strategic plan, plans from 5-7 key departments (e.g., Credit Operations, Risk, IT, Marketing, HR), and 10-15 interviews.
tests.controlTested: Effectiveness of strategic communication and organizational alignment mechanisms.

tests.title: Q3 2026 Strategic Work Plan Progress Verification
tests.objective: Verify actual progress against planned milestones, deliverables, and targets for key strategic initiatives within the Q3 2026 work plan.
tests.procedure: For a sample of 3-5 high-impact strategic initiatives/projects, obtain and review project status reports, evidence of milestone completion (e.g., system deployment reports, policy approval documents, new product launch data), and project meeting minutes.
tests.population: Q3 2026 strategic work plan, project documentation for key initiatives.
tests.sampleBasis: Targeted sample of 3-5 strategic initiatives identified as critical for Q3 2026 success.
tests.controlTested: Effectiveness of strategic work plan execution and progress tracking.

tests.name: Han
tests.title: Strategic Performance Monitoring & Reporting Review
tests.objective: Assess the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of strategic performance reports, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), against Q3 2026 targets.
tests.procedure: Obtain monthly/quarterly strategic performance reports for Q1 and Q2 2026. Select a sample of 5-7 key KPIs and trace reported data to underlying source systems or documentation to verify accuracy. Review evidence of report distribution and management review.
tests.population: Strategic performance reports (Q1, Q2 2026), underlying data sources (e.g., credit portfolio reports, customer acquisition dashboards, financial statements).
tests.sampleBasis: All Q1/Q2 strategic reports, a targeted sample of 5-7 critical KPIs.
tests.controlTested: Effectiveness of strategic performance monitoring and reporting controls.

tests.name: jkgfjkgjklfhjn
tests.title: Resource Allocation & Budget Alignment Analysis
tests.objective: Determine if financial, human, and technological resources are adequately allocated and aligned to support the execution of key Q3 2026 strategic initiatives.
tests.procedure: Review Q3 2026 budget allocations for strategic projects and initiatives. Compare allocated resources with stated requirements in project plans. Conduct interviews with project managers regarding resource sufficiency.
tests.population: Q3 2026 budget, project charters for strategic initiatives, HR records for key project staff.
tests.sampleBasis: Budget lines and project plans for the top 3 strategic initiatives by impact or spend.
tests.controlTested: Effectiveness of resource allocation processes in supporting strategic priorities.

tests.title: Strategic Risk Management Review
tests.objective: Evaluate the adequacy of CREDICORP's processes for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that could impact the achievement of Q3 2026 strategic objectives.
tests.procedure: Review CREDICORP's enterprise risk register, specific strategic risk assessments, and minutes from relevant risk committee or executive management meetings discussing strategic risks and their mitigation.
tests.population: Enterprise Risk Register, Strategic Risk Assessments, Risk Committee minutes.
tests.sampleBasis: All documented strategic risks identified for the period.
tests.controlTested: Effectiveness of strategic risk identification and mitigation controls.

keyRisks: Misalignment of Strategy with Market Realities: Strategic objectives may not adequately reflect the unique challenges and opportunities of the Nigerian consumer credit market (e.g., economic volatility, consumer behavior, regulatory changes).
Ineffective Strategy Execution: Failure to translate strategic objectives into actionable operational plans and projects, leading to gaps between intent and implementation.

Inadequate Performance Monitoring: Lack of timely, accurate, and relevant key performance indicators (KPIs) and reporting mechanisms to track progress against strategic objectives, hindering informed decision-making.
Resource Constraints and Misallocation: Insufficient or misdirected allocation of financial, human, or technological resources to critical strategic initiatives, impacting achievement of goals.

Regulatory Non-compliance Impacting Strategy: Strategic initiatives may inadvertently conflict with or fail to adequately address evolving Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) regulations or other financial sector requirements.
Lack of Organizational Buy-in: Insufficient communication or engagement across departments, leading to a lack of understanding, ownership, and commitment to strategic objectives.
objectives: Evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of CREDICORP's strategic planning and execution framework.
Assess CREDICORP's progress and performance against defined strategic objectives and the associated work plan for Q3 2026.
Determine the effectiveness of monitoring, reporting, and corrective action mechanisms for strategic performance.
Identify significant risks and challenges impacting the achievement of strategic goals for Q3 2026.
Provide recommendations to enhance strategic execution, oversight, and adaptation within CREDICORP.

plan.scope: The audit will cover the procurement processes, policies, procedures, and related internal controls within CREDICORP's Procurement Department for the period of Q3 2026. This includes requisitioning, vendor selection and management, competitive bidding, contract awarding, goods/services receipt, and payment initiation. The audit will not cover the operational effectiveness or financial health of third-party vendors, nor will it extend to procurement activities managed solely by other departments outside the Procurement Department's direct oversight.

tests.title: Review of Procurement Policy Compliance
tests.objective: To ascertain compliance with CREDICORP's approved procurement policies and procedures, including authorization limits and competitive bidding requirements.
tests.procedure: Obtain CREDICORP's procurement policy. Select a judgmental or statistical sample of procurement transactions. For each sample, verify that all necessary approvals were obtained, procurement methods (e.g., competitive bidding, single source) were appropriately followed and documented, and spending limits were adhered to.
tests.population: All procurement transactions initiated and/or completed within Q3 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Statistical sampling (e.g., monetary unit sampling) for high-value transactions; judgmental sampling for a mix of lower-value and specific transaction types.
tests.controlTested: Adherence to established procurement policies and approval matrices.

tests.title: Vendor Due Diligence and Qualification Review
tests.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of the vendor due diligence and qualification process to ensure credible and suitable vendors are engaged.
tests.procedure: Obtain the vendor onboarding policy. Select a sample of newly onboarded vendors or vendors awarded contracts during Q3 2026. For each sample, verify the completeness of vendor documentation (e.g., company registration, tax identification number, references, financial viability checks), and ensure the approval process for vendor registration was followed.
tests.population: All new vendor registrations or vendors awarded contracts in Q3 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgmental sample focusing on high-value vendors or a representative mix of vendor types.
tests.controlTested: Vendor due diligence, onboarding, and approval process.

tests.title: Analysis of Bidding and Quotation Process
tests.objective: To verify that competitive bidding principles are consistently applied to secure value for money and mitigate fraud risks.
tests.procedure: For a sample of procurements exceeding the competitive bidding threshold, review documentation to confirm that multiple bids/quotes were solicited (as per policy), bid opening procedures were followed, evaluation criteria were fair and documented, and the contract was awarded to the most advantageous bidder or justification for deviation was clearly recorded and approved.
tests.population: All procurement transactions exceeding the competitive bidding threshold in Q3 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Statistical sampling for high-value transactions.
tests.controlTested: Competitive bidding process, tender evaluation, and award authorization.

tests.title: Contract Performance and Amendment Verification
tests.objective: To ensure effective management of contracts, including monitoring performance and proper approval of any variations.
tests.procedure: Select a sample of active contracts or completed procurements from Q3 2026. Review contract files for evidence of performance monitoring (e.g., service level agreements, key performance indicators, periodic reviews). Verify that any contract amendments, extensions, or change orders were formally documented, justified, and duly approved according to policy.
tests.population: All active procurement contracts or procurements completed in Q3 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgmental sample focusing on long-term contracts, high-value contracts, or contracts with reported issues.
tests.controlTested: Contract management, monitoring, and amendment authorization.

tests.title: Goods/Services Receipt and Payment Authorization Review
tests.objective: To confirm that payments are made for goods/services that have been duly received, verified, and authorized.
tests.procedure: For a sample of payments processed during Q3 2026, reconcile invoices with approved purchase orders/contracts, goods receipt notes (GRNs) or service acceptance certificates (SACs). Verify that GRNs/SACs are properly authorized by the receiving department/user and that payment requests are approved by authorized personnel.
tests.population: All vendor payments processed for procurement activities in Q3 2026.
tests.sampleBasis: Statistical sampling focusing on higher-value payments.
tests.controlTested: Verification of goods/services receipt, invoice matching, and payment authorization.

tests.title: Assessment of Segregation of Duties (SoD)
tests.objective: To evaluate the adequacy of segregation of duties within the procurement process to prevent fraud and errors.
tests.procedure: Map key procurement process activities (e.g., requisition, vendor selection, PO creation, goods receipt, invoice approval, payment processing). Interview relevant personnel and review system access roles to confirm that incompatible functions are assigned to different individuals. Document any observed SoD conflicts or weaknesses.
tests.population: Procurement department staff, relevant system users, and process documentation.
tests.sampleBasis: Review of organizational charts, job descriptions, and system access logs for key personnel involved in the procurement process.
tests.controlTested: Segregation of duties across the procurement lifecycle.

keyRisks: Fraud and corruption (e.g., kickbacks, bid-rigging, favoritism) leading to financial loss and reputational damage.

Non-compliance with CREDICORP's internal procurement policies and procedures (e.g., unauthorized procurements, circumvention of competitive bidding) resulting in inefficient spending or control breakdowns.
Ineffective vendor selection and management, leading to poor quality goods/services, delays, or engagement with unsuitable vendors.
Lack of transparency and fairness in the procurement process, exposing CREDICORP to legal challenges and reputational risk.
Weak contract management leading to unapproved variations, cost overruns, or failure to receive contracted goods/services.
Non-compliance with relevant Nigerian regulatory requirements impacting procurement (e.g., tax laws, business registration) leading to penalties or legal issues.
objectives: To assess the effectiveness and efficiency of CREDICORP's procurement processes in achieving value for money.
To evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of internal controls governing procurement activities.
To determine CREDICORP's compliance with established procurement policies, procedures, and relevant regulatory requirements in Nigeria.
To identify and evaluate key risks associated with procurement and assess the mitigating controls in place.

audits.name: Test Audit Awa UAT - Legal Services Audit

observations.risk: The absence of perfected collateral significantly elevates CREDICORP's credit risk exposure, increasing the potential for substantial financial losses in the event of borrower default. This contravenes sound banking practices and can lead to difficulties in asset recovery, impacting the Corporation's profitability and capital adequacy. Additionally, it exposes CREDICORP to reputational damage and potential regulatory sanctions from the Central Bank of Nigeria for non-compliance with prudential lending guidelines.
observations.title: Absence of Perfected Collateral for Disbursed Loans
observations.criteria: CREDICORP's Credit Risk Management Policy (Section 4.2.1) mandates that all loans exceeding a defined threshold (e.g., NGN 5,000,000) must be secured by adequate and legally enforceable collateral. Furthermore, the Legal Services Department's Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) require the completion of collateral perfection prior to the final disbursement of any loan facility.
observations.rootCause:
Insufficient enforcement of CREDICORP's Credit Risk Management Policy regarding collateral requirements during the loan approval and disbursement stages.
Breakdown in communication and coordination between the Credit Operations and Legal Services Departments, leading to loans being disbursed without Legal Services confirming collateral perfection.
Potential for overrides of mandatory collateral requirements without appropriate compensatory controls or executive-level approvals.
observations.description: A review of 25 loan files disbursed between January and June 2024 revealed 9 (36%) instances where loans, totaling approximately NGN 150,000,000, were disbursed without adequate and legally perfected collateral as required by Corporation policy. Specifically, the documentation in these files indicated either no collateral was obtained, or the collateral offered was not fully perfected by Legal Services prior to loan disbursement, leaving CREDICORP's interest unsecured.
observations.recommendation:
Immediately halt disbursement of any new loans without documented and perfected collateral where required by policy. Review all recently disbursed loans to assess the collateral status and initiate perfection processes as needed.
Implement a mandatory pre-disbursement checklist and sign-off process, requiring explicit confirmation from Legal Services that all collateral associated with a loan facility has been fully perfected before funds are released.
Conduct joint training for Credit Operations and Legal Services staff to reinforce understanding of the collateral perfection process, roles, responsibilities, and the implications of non-compliance.
Evaluate and enhance the loan origination system to include automated controls or 'hard stops' that prevent disbursement of non-compliant loans.

observations.risk: The absence of formally documented Board meeting minutes poses significant regulatory, legal, and reputational risks for CREDICORP. It creates a critical vulnerability as it prevents the Corporation from demonstrating due diligence in its decision-making processes, particularly concerning credit approvals, risk management, and strategic direction. This non-compliance with CAMA 2020 and internal policies could lead to regulatory sanctions, legal challenges from stakeholders due to lack of verifiable evidence of decisions, potential misinterpretation or non-implementation of Board directives, and an inability to provide an auditable trail for corporate actions. This constitutes a major control failure impacting corporate governance and compliance.
observations.title: Absence of Formal Documentation for Board of Directors Meeting Minutes
observations.criteria: The Corporation's Board Charter stipulates that all Board of Directors meetings must be formally documented, signed off by the Chairman and Company Secretary, and retained as official records. Furthermore, Section 261(1) of the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020 mandates the proper keeping of minutes of all general meetings and board meetings of a company. CREDICORP's internal Record Management Policy (Section 3.2.1) also requires comprehensive documentation of all critical corporate decisions and proceedings.
observations.rootCause:
Inadequate understanding of the strict regulatory and internal requirements for formal minute documentation and retention by relevant personnel.
Lack of a clearly defined, consistent, and enforced process within the Legal Department for timely preparation, review, and sign-off of Board minutes post-meeting.
Potential resource constraints or competing priorities within the Legal Department impacting the timely completion of minute-taking duties.
observations.description: During the review of corporate governance records held by the Legal Department, it was observed that formal minutes were not consistently documented for certain Board of Directors meetings conducted within the audit period (e.g., Q1 and Q2 2024). Specifically, for three out of five Board meetings reviewed, only informal notes or draft outlines were available, lacking official sign-off by the Company Secretary and Board Chair. This indicates a significant gap in the official record-keeping of critical decisions and discussions, hindering proper governance oversight.
observations.agreedTarget: Within 30 days, implement revised process and commence retrospective documentation for all identified outstanding minutes.
observations.recommendation:
Establish and enforce a robust, documented procedure for the preparation, review, sign-off, and archiving of Board of Directors meeting minutes within 7 working days of each meeting, clearly assigning responsibilities.
Conduct mandatory training for the Company Secretary's office and relevant Legal Department staff on the regulatory and corporate governance requirements for minute-keeping, emphasizing the criticality of formal documentation and compliance.
Implement a tracking mechanism to ensure all Board meetings have corresponding formally approved minutes, complete with assigned responsibilities and deadlines, to monitor compliance.
Ensure all outstanding undocumented Board meetings within the audit scope are formally documented and ratified retrospectively by the Board where possible, or clearly noted in subsequent minutes.

plan.scope: The audit will evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of CREDICORP's Risk Management Department (RMD) in fulfilling its mandate of identifying, assessing, monitoring, and mitigating key enterprise risks across the institution for the period covering the past 12-18 months. It will cover the RMD's governance structure, policies, processes, systems, staffing, and compliance with regulatory requirements. The audit will not delve into the granular credit decisions or operational risk events managed directly by individual business units, but rather the RMD's oversight, framework, and reporting capabilities for these areas.

tests.name: Review of Risk Management Framework & Policies
tests.title: Review of Risk Management Framework & Policies
tests.control: Existence, comprehensiveness, and formal approval of the risk management framework and policies.
tests.objective: To evaluate the comprehensiveness, clarity, and approval status of CREDICORP's enterprise risk management framework, policies, and procedures.
tests.procedure: Obtain and review the RMD's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, risk management policies (e.g., credit risk, operational risk, market risk, liquidity risk), and related procedures. Compare these documents against CBN prudential guidelines for DFIs and industry best practices. Verify formal approval by relevant committees (e.g., Board Risk Committee).
tests.population: All RMD-owned policy documents, ERM framework document, Board/committee minutes approving these.
tests.sampleBasis: 100% review of core ERM framework and key risk policies (Credit, Operational, Market, Liquidity).
tests.controlTested: Existence, comprehensiveness, and formal approval of the risk management framework and policies.

tests.name: Effectiveness of Risk Identification & Assessment
tests.title: Effectiveness of Risk Identification & Assessment
tests.control: Risk identification methodology, risk assessment process, and maintenance of risk registers.
tests.objective: To assess the robustness of the RMD's processes for identifying, assessing, and documenting key enterprise risks.
tests.procedure: Review the latest enterprise-wide risk register(s), risk appetite statement, and significant risk assessment reports. Interview RMD staff and key business unit risk owners to understand the risk identification methodology. Trace a sample of identified risks from initial identification to assessment and inclusion in the risk register.
tests.population: Enterprise Risk Register, departmental risk registers, risk workshops minutes, significant risk assessment reports from the past 12-18 months.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgmental selection of 5-10 high-impact or recently identified risks, and 3-5 departmental risk registers.
tests.controlTested: Risk identification methodology, risk assessment process, and maintenance of risk registers.

tests.name: Review of Risk Monitoring & Mitigation Activities
tests.title: Review of Risk Monitoring & Mitigation Activities
tests.control: Risk monitoring processes, KRI tracking, and effectiveness of mitigation action follow-up.
tests.objective: To confirm the effectiveness of the RMD's ongoing risk monitoring processes and the implementation of agreed-upon risk mitigation actions.
tests.procedure: Obtain and review RMD's risk monitoring reports, key risk indicator (KRI) dashboards, and records of risk limit breaches. For a sample of reported breaches or high-priority risks, verify that appropriate mitigation actions were agreed upon, assigned, and tracked by the RMD and business units. Confirm follow-up on overdue actions.
tests.population: Monthly/Quarterly Risk Reports, KRI dashboards, minutes of risk committee meetings, records of risk limit breaches and corresponding action plans for the past 12-18 months.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgmental selection of 3-5 significant risk limit breaches or high-priority risks with associated mitigation plans.
tests.controlTested: Risk monitoring processes, KRI tracking, and effectiveness of mitigation action follow-up.

tests.name: Accuracy & Timeliness of Risk Reporting
tests.title: Accuracy & Timeliness of Risk Reporting
tests.control: Accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of internal and external risk reporting.
tests.objective: To assess the reliability, completeness, and timeliness of risk reports submitted to senior management and the Board.
tests.procedure: Obtain copies of risk reports presented to the Board Risk Committee and Executive Management Committee over the audit period. Trace key risk figures (e.g., NPL ratio, operational loss events, market risk exposures) from selected reports back to source data (e.g., core banking system reports, financial statements). Verify adherence to reporting schedules.
tests.population: All Board Risk Committee and Executive Management Committee risk packs/reports over the past 12-18 months.
tests.sampleBasis: Judgmental selection of 3-4 comprehensive quarterly or bi-annual risk reports.
tests.controlTested: Accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of internal and external risk reporting.

tests.name: Compliance with Regulatory Requirements
tests.title: Compliance with Regulatory Requirements
tests.control: RMD's compliance monitoring process and adherence to regulatory requirements.
tests.objective: To verify CREDICORP's adherence to relevant CBN prudential guidelines and other regulatory directives concerning risk management.
tests.procedure: Review relevant CBN circulars and directives related to risk management for DFIs. Map the RMD's processes and controls against these requirements. Obtain and review evidence of compliance (e.g., self-assessment reports, internal/external audit findings related to regulatory compliance, RMD responses to regulatory examinations).
tests.population: Applicable CBN circulars, internal compliance reports, regulatory examination reports, RMD self-assessment documentation.
tests.sampleBasis: 100% review of key CBN guidelines for DFI risk management; judgmental selection of 2-3 compliance self-assessments or regulatory responses.
tests.controlTested: RMD's compliance monitoring process and adherence to regulatory requirements.

tests.name: RMD Staffing and Competence Assessment
tests.title: RMD Staffing and Competence Assessment
tests.control: Adequacy of human resources, staff competence, and continuous professional development.
tests.objective: To evaluate the adequacy of RMD staffing levels, organizational structure, and staff technical competence relative to the institution's risk profile.
tests.procedure: Review the RMD's organizational chart, job descriptions, and staff professional qualification/training records. Interview RMD senior management regarding succession planning and skill gaps. Benchmark staffing levels and expertise against similar DFIs or industry standards where available.
tests.population: RMD organizational structure, staff training records, HR policies on recruitment and training, budget allocations for RMD.
tests.sampleBasis: 100% review of RMD structure and key job descriptions; judgmental review of training records for 5-7 key RMD personnel across different risk areas.
tests.controlTested: Adequacy of human resources, staff competence, and continuous professional development.

keyRisks: Inadequate identification or assessment of emerging or material risks (e.g., credit portfolio deterioration, technology risks, regulatory changes) impacting CREDICORP's strategic objectives and financial stability.
Failure to establish or effectively enforce robust risk management policies, procedures, and limits, leading to excessive risk exposure or control breakdowns.
Untimely, inaccurate, or incomplete risk reporting to senior management and the Board, hindering effective decision-making and oversight.
Non-compliance with relevant regulatory requirements (e.g., CBN guidelines on risk management, IFRS 9 credit provisioning) due to deficiencies in the RMD's processes or oversight.
Insufficient resources, technical expertise, or training within the RMD to effectively manage the breadth and complexity of risks faced by a Development Finance Institution (DFI).
Lack of effective integration of risk management activities across business units, leading to siloed risk views and inconsistent application of risk controls.
objectives: Evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of the Risk Management Department's (RMD) framework, policies, and procedures for identifying, assessing, mitigating, and monitoring key enterprise risks, including credit, operational, market, and liquidity risks.
Assess the RMD's compliance with established internal risk management policies, relevant Nigerian regulatory requirements (e.g., CBN guidelines for DFIs), and international best practices.
Determine the reliability, completeness, and timeliness of risk reporting to senior management and the Board, and the effectiveness of their risk oversight based on these reports.
Review the adequacy of the RMD's staffing, resources, and technical expertise in relation to the scale and complexity of CREDICORP's risk profile.

observations.risk: Inaccurate and untimely risk reporting can lead to misinformed strategic decisions, impaired oversight by the Board and Executive Management, and a failure to adequately manage and mitigate emerging risks. This exposes CREDICORP to undetected significant financial losses, non-compliance with regulatory reporting requirements, reputational damage, and an increased likelihood of regulatory sanctions or fines, thereby jeopardizing the Corporation's financial stability and strategic objectives.
observations.title: Inaccuracies and Untimeliness in Board and Executive Risk Reports
observations.criteria: CREDICORP's 'Risk Reporting Policy' (Section 3.1) mandates that all risk reports submitted to senior management and the Board must be accurate, complete, and submitted according to approved reporting schedules to facilitate timely and informed decision-making. The policy requires submission within 5 working days post-period-end and a zero-tolerance for material inaccuracies.
observations.rootCause:
Inadequate validation and quality assurance processes for risk data aggregation and reporting prior to submission.
Reliance on manual data compilation methods, increasing the potential for human error and delays.
Insufficient staffing or training within the Risk Management Department to meet reporting demands and ensure consistent quality control.
Weaknesses in inter-departmental data reconciliation processes, particularly between the Risk Management Department and source data providers (e.g., Finance, Operations).
observations.description: During the audit period, a review of selected comprehensive quarterly and bi-annual risk reports submitted to the Board Risk Committee and Executive Management Committee revealed instances of material inaccuracies and untimely submissions. Specifically, for two out of four selected reports, key risk figures such as the Non-Performing Loan (NPL) ratio and reported operational loss events exhibited variances ranging from 5% to 15% when traced back to source data from the core banking system and financial statements. Furthermore, three of the four selected reports were submitted between 5 to 10 working days beyond the established internal deadlines, impacting the promptness of executive and board oversight.
observations.recommendation:
Implement a robust, documented, and regularly performed validation and quality assurance process for all key risk figures prior to report finalization and submission.
Investigate and procure an automated risk reporting solution to minimize manual intervention, enhance data integrity, and improve reporting timeliness.
Review and update the 'Risk Reporting Policy' to explicitly define accountability for data accuracy and reporting timeliness, including clear escalation procedures for delays or discrepancies.
Provide targeted training to Risk Management Department staff on data extraction, aggregation, reconciliation, and quality assurance techniques.
Establish formal Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with data-providing departments (e.g., Finance, Operations, IT) to ensure timely and accurate source data provision to the Risk Management Department.

1.1.gap: The organizational structure creates a perceived and potential actual limitation on the professional courage needed to challenge management effectively, especially within IT.
1.1.action: Establish a direct functional reporting line to the Audit Committee or Board to reinforce independence and professional courage.
1.1.evidence: Audit reports reflect findings, but the reporting line to Head IT may subtly influence professional courage on sensitive IT-related matters.

1.2.evidence: IA staff are aware of and generally adhere to CREDICORP's code of conduct and ethical policies.

1.3.evidence: There are no known instances of IA staff violating applicable laws, regulations, or professional ethical guidelines.
